title: sparq-zk-inference: in-circuit ZK-over-hidden-antecedent derivation_step member (RDFS-first)
description:

HONEST STATUS: this is GREENFIELD Noir. NO derivation/entailment .nr exists in zk/compose/compose_core/src/ today. What ships (derivation.rs + verifier.rs:4401 bind_entailment) is a HOST-SIDE structural re-check over DISCLOSED scan rows (verifiable correctness, ZERO antecedent privacy, NOT a ZK proof). The skeleton + the witness source are reused; the in-circuit RELATION is brand-new.

DELIVER (opt-in sparq-zk-inference crate or zk-inference feature):
1. new in-circuit derivation_step member per ProofNode: rule's fixed variable-sharing equalities over term encodings (~10^2 gates/node by judgement — CONFIRM with `bb gates` before any cost claim).
2. premise/conclusion term-encodings chained by encoding-equality for internal DAG nodes.
3. DAG-leaf antecedents anchored to membership-against-commitments[g] via scan.nr's set-membership accumulator (the privacy upgrade + soundness anchor) — REPLACES 'antecedent == disclosed row'.
4. zk-trace mapper: sparq-reason explain why()->ProofTree (flat premises-before-conclusion DAG, ExplainOpts{max_depth:128,max_nodes:65536}) -> witness slot indices; one ProofTree per derived disclosed row.

RULE SCOPE v1: extend EntailmentRule from the shipped two (rdfs7/rdfs9) to rdfs2/rdfs3/rdfs5/rdfs11 (same fixed shape). owl:sameAs is SEPARATE (sq-rsd3v.7) — encoding-equality is UNSOUND under equality reasoning.

title: Single-use nullifier primitive (in-circuit Poseidon2(hsk, epoch)) — the one genuinely-absent ZK gadget
description:
The ONE genuinely-absent primitive in the estate (grep across sparq-zk + sparq-zk-compose finds no nullifier/double-spend). Prerequisite for unlinkable presentation (sq-wvne) AND delegation non-replayability (sq-l5og).

NOT a 'generalised audit-#4 store'. The shipped audit-#4 nonce binding is purely verifier-side (every circuit does `let _ = challenge;`; binding = public-input field-0 byte-compare). The nullifier is NEW in-circuit soundness surface:
(a) nf = Poseidon2([ZKSIG_NF, hsk, epoch]) computed IN-CIRCUIT from the WITNESSED hsk, asserted equal to public nf (new ZKSIG_NF domain tag in crates/sparq-zk/src/sig.rs).
(b) soundness rides BOTH the holder-PoK DL-binding of hsk (NOT-yet-sound, sq-qhy4) AND Poseidon2 domain-separated collision-resistance over (ZKSIG_NF, hsk, epoch).
(c) GRANULARITY claimed = per-holder-per-epoch rate-limit (nf binds hsk+epoch but NOT the credential/commitment, so one key across distinct credentials in one epoch COLLIDES). It is NOT a per-presentation single-use token; a per-presentation variant folds the commitment in and is a SEPARATE larger obligation.
(d) double-spend enforcement = verifier-side seen-set of nf per epoch, fail-closed on collision.

DELIVER: zk-nullifier opt-in feature; the new in-circuit gadget + ZKSIG_NF tag + verifier seen-set gate; forge-and-verify regression test (replay same nf in same epoch must fail-closed). Honest scope notes per research/zk-inference-and-credentials.md §6.3. NOT-yet-sound (sq-qhy4). [OPUS-4.8]

title: Structure-aware vectorisation + flexible grounding (opt-in over sparq-vectors/shacl/reason)
description:
EPIC: Structure-aware vectorisation + flexible grounding for sparq (opt-in, over sparq-vectors + sparq-shacl + sparq-reason).

Design record: research/structure-aware-vectorisation.md

CORE THESIS: structural/ontological properties of a KG are PRIORS over the embedding manifold, not post-hoc filters. Make a node vector a STRUCTURED PARTITIONED OBJECT — a concatenation of typed sub-vectors whose geometry is chosen by structure (Euclidean free attrs, hyperbolic/box taxonomy, order-preserving magnitudes, codebook enums, sign booleans) and whose training is regularised by closed+declared axioms. The same object is the unit of FLEXIBLE GROUNDING: return the minimal-and-complete object in whatever modality the consumer needs (typed sub-vector / subgraph / NL string / typed value). Inherited invariant: opt-in, never serves exact BGP answers, only proposes candidates the exact engine re-validates.

HONESTY POSTURE (load-bearing): order-preservation (RESTRICTED quantile+strictly-monotone encoder ONLY — NOT a "monotone Fourier-feature map", which is periodic/non-monotone under cosine), enum/boolean exactness, and PROFILE-RELATIVE closure completeness are FORMALLY PROVABLE. Embedding quality is EMPIRICAL and dataset-dependent; the literal/type-aware KGE literature reports INCONSISTENT gains (Gesese et al. 2021; LiteralE ISWC-2019). Every prior ships behind an on/off ablation and is adopted only on measured lift. NO benchmark numbers exist yet. NO ZK/MPC claim.

=== MAINTAINER'S RAW REQUEST (verbatim, all four messages) ===

(1) "How would you approach vectorising a knowledge graph in a way that takes account of its structural and ontological properties — e.g. that some predicate ranges are enumerations, some are integers, some have a declared domain/range, there is a subclass hierarchy, etc.?"

(2) "Assess the quality of the approach — via formal results and/or benchmarks."

(3) "When such a vectorisation is used for grounding (e.g. an LLM tool call), the grounding need not be a subgraph — it could be a vector, an NL string, or some other object the consumer needs. Consider that."

(4) "Consider how different inference techniques — structured (deductive/constraint) and unstructured (neural/similarity) — interplay here."

=== PHASED PLAN (prioritised, cheapest/lowest-risk first) ===
P0 closure-before-vectorise + type-constrained negative sampling (STRONGEST/SAFEST; no format/serving change)
P1 typed literal encoders (datatype router + order-preserving numeric + boolean-sign + date/Timeline) + schema header + per-block metric tags
P2 enum/datatype/cardinality prior extraction from sparq-shacl + QUDT unit-normalisation
P3 taxonomy block (Euclidean default; hyperbolic/box ONLY past a measured-distortion gate) + disjointness repulsion/mask; gUFO rigid/role split optional/last
P4 flexible minimal-complete grounding selector + verbaliser (subgraph/vector/NL/typed-value)
P5 neuro-symbolic propose(neural)-then-verify(deductive) pipeline (sparq-reason <-> sparq-vectors)
P6 eval harness + formal-properties write-up

Child beads track P0..P6. [OPUS-4.8]

title: Security-properties ontology for ZK proofs/systems (unlinkability, PQ-security, soundness, ZK-ness, ...) — machine-reasonable, ODRL-privacy-preference-driven proof admissibility, wired into sparq-zk per-method + trust-graph PoC
description:
RAW MAINTAINER REQUEST (verbatim, 2026-06-20):
"For the trust graph, can you deep research literature and existing ontologies to see what already exists on this front, and whether there is anything that can be sensibly built upon and integrated into the PoC. When it comes to the security properties you are describing, I would like to have an ontology to describe the security properties of a given system / proof; that can be used to reason e.g. about what proofs can/cannot be used based on privacy preferences that a user has expressed using ODRL. This should capture things like unlinkability, post quantum security, etc. I had already thought about and built some of this out in the context of the work I had previously done with zero knowledge proof and SPARQL. Can you build this in and use it in the appropriate places. Can you also provide a critical evaluation of what the right next steps for things to build out in this area are"

INTERPRETATION / SCOPE:
1. DEEP RESEARCH: existing literature + ontologies for (a) trust/authorization graphs (to integrate into the PoC) and (b) SECURITY/PRIVACY PROPERTIES of proofs+systems (unlinkability, PQ-security, ZK soundness, hiding/binding, anonymity-set, etc.). Identify what can be sensibly built upon.
2. CRITICALLY fold in the maintainer's OWN prior ZK+SPARQL security-properties work (lws-acp docs + his zk/sparql repos + ISWC/blog/transfer sources; 'a lot of that could be crap' — be critical).
3. DESIGN a security-properties ontology that an N3/ODRL reasoner can use to decide proof ADMISSIBILITY from a user's ODRL-expressed privacy preferences (e.g. 'require unlinkable + PQ-secure' -> admissible proof set).
4. WIRE IT IN: annotate each sparq-zk cryptosuite/commitment/circuit method with its security properties; use it in the trust-graph PoC admission gate (crates/sparq-trust) as the proof-selection/admissibility check; this is the machine-readable realization of the #890(b) ZK<->ODRL envelope (sq-yh427) and supersedes the prose #919 per-method write-up.
5. CRITICAL EVALUATION of the right next steps to build out.
SEQUENCE: deep-research+design record (maintainer review) FIRST, then impl. Relates: sq-pfae (trust-graph), sq-1s2.5 (ZK cryptosuite framework), #919 (prose security-properties), sq-yh427 (ZK<->ODRL envelope), sq-qhy4 (ZK estate unaudited — no production security claim). [OPUS-4.8]

title: JSON-LD compaction: @reverse edge to a non-subject object is silently dropped (data loss)
description:
🤖 SPARQ agent — confirmed by adversarial audit of PR #950 (JSON-LD 1.1 Compaction). [OPUS-4.8]

SILENT DATA LOSS (high). `relocate_reverse` deletes a forward edge covered by a `@reverse`
term from EVERY subject, but only re-attaches edges whose object node appears as a subject
in the same graph — so an edge to an object that is never itself a subject is dropped.

Location: crates/sparq-engine/src/serialize/compact.rs:625-695.
- Lines 638-642 build `index` from subject @ids only.
- Lines 653-658 add an edge to `moves` ONLY when `index.get(oid)` is Some.
- Lines 666-670 unconditionally `members.retain(...)` to remove the reverse-term IRI from
  ALL subject nodes once `moves` is non-empty.
Net effect: if any reverse edge relocates (so the bulk `retain` runs), a parallel reverse
edge whose object is a pure object (never a subject) is stripped from its subject and never
re-added anywhere.

REACHABLE ON THE REAL RDF PATH (needs >=2 reverse edges so `moves` is non-empty):
  <http://ex/alice> <http://ex/knows> <http://ex/bob> .
  <http://ex/bob>   <http://ex/name>  "Bob" .
  <http://ex/eve>   <http://ex/knows> <http://ex/frank> .
Context: {"@vocab":"http://ex/","id":"@id","name":"http://ex/name",
          "knownBy":{"@reverse":"http://ex/knows"}}

sparq output: eve becomes {"id":"http://ex/eve"} — the eve->frank edge GONE.
pyld (W3C reference): {"id":"http://ex/eve","knows":{"id":"http://ex/frank"}} — preserved.

(Note: the single-edge case in the original repro does NOT lose data, because `moves` is
empty and the function early-returns before the bulk retain. The loss requires a second,
relocatable reverse edge — this mixed case is the real trigger.)

Spec ref: W3C JSON-LD 1.1 Compaction §node compaction / @reverse handling. A reverse edge
to a non-subject object should still be expressible (the reference keeps it as the forward
property; it must never be silently removed).

Confirming test (throwaway harness, not committed):
crates/sparq-engine/tests/compact_audit_confirm.rs ::
  s5_reverse_to_nonsubject_DATA_LOSS_CONFIRMED

Fix sketch: only remove a forward edge from a subject when that specific edge was actually
relocated (track removed edges per subject/object), OR materialise a stub node for an
object that is not yet a subject so the edge has a home; never strip edges that were not
re-attached.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #963 (https://github.com/jeswr/sparq/pull/963) [OPUS-4.8]: spec-correct compaction + permanent regression test asserting the pyld-verified output and the losslessness round-trip.

title: JSON-LD compaction: @language container drops values lacking a language tag (data loss)
description:
🤖 SPARQ agent — confirmed by adversarial audit of PR #950 (JSON-LD 1.1 Compaction). [OPUS-4.8]

SILENT DATA LOSS (high in effect). `@language`-container compaction drops any value that is
not a string-typed, language-tagged literal.

Location: crates/sparq-engine/src/serialize/compact.rs:735-746. The loop only inserts items
for which BOTH `v.get("@value").and_then(Json::as_str)` AND
`v.get("@language").and_then(Json::as_str)` succeed. A value lacking a language tag (e.g. a
numeric/typed literal) — or whose @value is not a JSON string — is silently skipped and
never emitted anywhere.

REACHABLE ON THE REAL RDF PATH:
  @prefix ex: <http://ex/> .
  ex:s ex:labels "Hello"@en .
  ex:s ex:labels 42 .
Context: {"labels":{"@id":"http://ex/labels","@container":"@language"}}

sparq output: {"@graph":[{"@id":"http://ex/s","labels":{"en":"Hello"}}]}  — 42 GONE.
pyld (W3C reference): {"labels":{"en":"Hello","@none":42}}  — 42 preserved under @none.

LOSSLESSNESS VIOLATION (decisive): sparq's output round-tripped through pyld toRdf yields
only `"Hello"@en`; the triple `<http://ex/s> <http://ex/labels> "42"^^xsd:integer` is lost.

Spec ref: https://www.w3.org/TR/json-ld11-api/#compaction-algorithm (language-map framing;
items that do not fit the map fall to an `@none` member, they are NOT dropped).

Confirming test (throwaway harness, not committed):
crates/sparq-engine/tests/compact_audit_confirm.rs ::
  s3_language_container_nonstring_DATA_LOSS_CONFIRMED

Fix sketch: collect items that lack a usable @language (or non-string @value) into an
`@none` bucket and emit them (array form per the spec) instead of discarding them.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #963 (https://github.com/jeswr/sparq/pull/963) [OPUS-4.8]: spec-correct compaction + permanent regression test asserting the pyld-verified output and the losslessness round-trip.

title: JSON-LD compaction: @list container drops co-located non-list values (data loss)
description:
🤖 SPARQ agent — confirmed by adversarial audit of PR #950 (JSON-LD 1.1 Compaction). [OPUS-4.8]

SILENT DATA LOSS (high). `@list`-container compaction in `compact_property` discards
co-located values.

Location: crates/sparq-engine/src/serialize/compact.rs:723-731. When a term has
`@container: @list`, the code does `items.iter().find_map(|v| v.get("@list"))` and emits
ONLY the unwrapped list, ignoring every other item in the property's object array. The W3C
spec (JSON-LD 1.1 Compaction §4.1) requires the `@list` framing to apply only to the list
value(s); any sibling non-list value must still be emitted (the reference processor pyld
keeps it under the expanded property IRI).

REACHABLE ON THE REAL RDF PATH (not a synthetic expanded doc):
  @prefix ex: <http://ex/> .
  ex:s ex:prop ( "a" "b" ) .
  ex:s ex:prop "c" .
Context: {"items":{"@id":"http://ex/prop","@container":"@list"}}

sparq output: {"@graph":[{"@id":"http://ex/s","items":["a","b"]}]}  — "c" GONE.
pyld (W3C reference): {"items":["a","b"],"http://ex/prop":"c"}  — "c" preserved.

LOSSLESSNESS VIOLATION (decisive): running sparq's emitted document through pyld toRdf
reconstructs ONLY the rdf:List (a,b); the triple `<http://ex/s> <http://ex/prop> "c"` is
permanently lost. This directly contradicts the module's documented losslessness guarantee.

Spec ref: https://www.w3.org/TR/json-ld11-api/#compaction-algorithm (container framing).

Confirming test (throwaway harness, not committed):
crates/sparq-engine/tests/compact_audit_confirm.rs ::
  s2_list_container_multi_value_DATA_LOSS_CONFIRMED

Fix sketch: in the `@list` branch, only unwrap the list value(s); compact remaining
non-list items via the normal value/node path and emit them too (matching pyld). Guard the
unwrap so it does not swallow siblings.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #963 (https://github.com/jeswr/sparq/pull/963) [OPUS-4.8]: spec-correct compaction + permanent regression test asserting the pyld-verified output and the losslessness round-trip.

title: Trust-graph open problem: delegation invocation-binding gate (invoker == terminal delegate, key-proven) is unspecified — admitted delegation is replayable
description: OPEN SECURITY PROBLEM from adversarial review of research/solid-trust-graph-authz-design.md §4. UCAN/ZCAP separate DELEGATION (the signed chain doc) from INVOCATION (exercising it, key-bound to THIS request). The doc §4.1 models a delegation as a trusted-source-attested graph fact riding the admission rail — that captures the chain's EXISTENCE but NOT the per-request invoker binding. §3.4 gives holder binding for ATTRIBUTE credentials (credentialSubject==Session.agent) but the doc NEVER states the delegation analogue: authenticated invoker == chain terminal delegate, key-proven per request. Without it, an admitted delegation becomes a standing graph fact ANY session reaching that graph can ride = replay/re-delegation escalation, same severity class as the §2.4 boundary re-opening. COMPOUNDING: there is ZERO delegation/key-proof substrate today — grep across sparq-solid+sparq-server finds no dpop/gnap/zcap/ucan/proof-of-possession; Session.client is a bare IRI with no PoP; sparq-prov records single-agent prov:wasAssociatedWith, NOT actedOnBehalfOf. Also §4.1 'admitted-as-graph-fact' (ambient) is in TENSION with §4.3 'carry-with-invocation, no ambient lookup'. SPECIFY: the invocation-binding rule + key-proof (DPoP/GNAP) layer; add delegation-replay adversarial forgery tests (analogue of acp_forged_*_in_acr_document_does_not_grant). Blocks-relation: prerequisite for sq-pfae.6 (P5). [OPUS-4.8]

title: Trust-graph open problem: per-request holder-binding/freshness admission vs session-independent materialize-once auth view
description: OPEN SOUNDNESS PROBLEM surfaced by adversarial review of research/solid-trust-graph-authz-design.md. The shipped sparq-solid auth view is materialized ONCE session-independently (PodStore, lib.rs) and queried per-session by principal expansion. But the trust-graph admission stratum gates on credentialSubject==Session.agent (holder binding, §3.4) and trust:freshWithin vs Session.now — both PER-REQUEST facts. Admission therefore cannot sit as a clean pre-derivation stratum inside the materialize-once view: either it re-runs per request (negating the P4 epoch-cache composition / sq-pfae.5) or holder binding degrades to a query-time principal match. The doc §3.3/§7 presented per-request admission as a clean stratification without reconciling this. NOTE: per-request 'now' IS already consulted for time-windowed conditional grants (authindex.rs sq-0q7n), which is a partial precedent, but per-request IDENTITY-bound admission ahead of derivation is unspecified. Decide: (a) split static-admission (signature/type-scope, materialize-time) from dynamic-admission (holder-binding/freshness, query-time), or (b) per-request re-materialize for credential-gated resources. [OPUS-4.8]

title: P3: claim-level admission stratum (closes acp:vc gap)
description: CORE DELIVERABLE. N3 admission rules + Rust wiring that verify an issuer signature over a credential's RDFC-1.0 commitment, check trust:trustsSourceFor, freshness, and the subject-to-requester holder binding, then inject admitted issuer-tagged facts AHEAD of the sparq-solid materialiser. Reuse sparq-canon, sparq-zk/sig, the solidx:/urn:sparq: reserved-predicate guards. SOUNDNESS: never admit on a self-asserted trust triple — verified signature only; enforce statement-type scoping at admission; add adversarial forgery tests mirroring acp_forged_*_in_acr_document_does_not_grant. Blocked-on P1(sq-pfae.2)+P2(sq-pfae.3). [OPUS-4.8]

title: feat(sparq-server/sparq-serve): online consistent snapshot backup + restore for the serving store (gated /admin/backup + /admin/restore, feature `backup`) — maintainer #905 green light
description:
Maintainer @jeswr GREEN LIGHT on #905 (real-voice comment, bare 'Green light'; issue body is the SPARQ-agent proposal). Implement ONLINE backup/restore of the in-memory serving store. Export an already-immutable pinned generation (triples + dict + per-pod epoch vectors + writer seq) to a durable artifact WHILE SERVING (no stop-the-world; readers never block writer, writer never blocks readers).

Surface: sparq-serve owns the generation-ring export/import (ring.rs / writer.rs / epoch.rs / applier.rs); sparq-server adds gated `POST /admin/backup` + `/admin/restore` admin routes; restore-from-artifact also runs on start.

CONSTRAINTS (all from the proposal body, greenlit as-stated): (1) OPT-IN behind a `backup` feature — serving core stays buildable without it. (2) Distinct from offline `sparq-cli save` (stop-the-world, index rebuild) AND from the per-graph WAL (persisted-graph path) — both verified NOT to cover this. (3) Artifact format: go with Option A (single self-describing backup artifact, Stardog backup-ID model) for v1 — agent's recommendation, NOT overridden by jeswr; Option B (reuse WAL-backed directory openable by query-mmap) couples to persisted-graph layout and is rejected for v1. This format choice also shapes the future change-stream/PITR companions. (4) At-rest encryption of the artifact is OUT OF SCOPE / a separate concern (research/crypto-erase-at-rest.md is design-only) — do not imply it. (5) Restore is the bootstrap primitive for the horizontal-scaling ADR stage-2 and the base half of PITR. (6) Benchmark numbers on this -aws work-box are NON-CANONICAL — don't bake throughput into docs/tests.

SERIALIZE on sparq-server (one serving-feature PR at a time). Tag [OPUS-4.8] on new code/notes; self-identify as SPARQ agent on the PR.
close_reason: Implemented online consistent snapshot backup + restore (sparq-serve backup module + sparq-server gated /admin/backup + /admin/restore + --restore on start, feature `backup` OFF by default). title: feat(sparq-serve): response-bytes result cache over PodEpochs (canonical-query x visibility-scope x epoch key, single-flight, off by default)
description:
jeswr GREEN-LIGHT on #904 (verbatim: 'Green light, please proceed'). Execute the already-RECOMMEND-verdict design in research/concurrent-serving.md §5 row 2 + §6.3 (cache layer NOT yet implemented; only PodEpochs/epoch.rs + Cache-Control headers exist in sparq-serve).

KEY CONTRACT (non-negotiable): key = (canonical-query hash x visibility-scope hash x per-pod epoch-vector hash). Visibility-scope keying is a CORRECTNESS/access-control obligation (never WebID; use AuthIndex::accessible identity, Hasura lesson) so cached bytes never cross an access-control boundary — NOT itself a privacy guarantee. Invalidation = per-pod (per-named-graph) epoch bumps, NOT precise dependency tracking; entry records max epoch of touched graphs; unbounded-footprint queries key on the global generation. Add single-flight/lease dedup (one execution, N waiters — the only MQO survivor). Bounded byte-budget LRU + admission (size cap; never cache streaming/oversize results). Canonicalization starts cheap: whitespace/prefix normalization + variable renaming; measure hit-rate before going further.

OFF BY DEFAULT (opt-in feature) — gate must pass in BOTH feature states; default-OFF feature-state test required. Respect library-first rule (sparq-serve sync, runtime-agnostic, no HTTP/async types in API; async adapters behind a feature flag only) and the sparq-wasm dependency-direction guard (cargo tree -p sparq-wasm -e normal | grep -c serve == 0). Sub-plan/semantic (QLever subtree) caching is OUT OF SCOPE for v1. DIFFERENT layer from sparq-engine/src/cache.rs (the embedded whole-query algebra-keyed LRU).

BENCHMARK-GATED: scheduler+epoch machinery <=1% overhead vs baseline + all-distinct adversary <=0.2us/req; the work-box here is NON-CANONICAL and cannot produce the canonical throughput numbers (4.8M->23.8M ops/s class) the design cites — flag any perf claim accordingly and defer canonical validation to a canonical host. Opus 4.8 trailer + [OPUS-4.8] markers; PR (not push); SPARQ-agent self-id blockquote. SERIALIZE on the serving surface (one serving-feature PR at a time).

title: bench.yml auto-ratchet push HEAD:main fails on protected branch — perf-baseline floor never lands on main (red push:main runs)
description: The bench.yml 'Auto-ratchet the perf floor' step (sq-52e) does git commit + 'git push HEAD:main' with the default GITHUB_TOKEN, same pattern as the bead-autoclose bug (sq-roe3). On push:main it FAILS with a non-fast-forward rejection ('! [rejected] HEAD -> main (fetch first)') because main moved ahead of the runner checkout during the long bench job; it would ALSO be GH013-rejected by the main ruleset (id 17688455: pull_request + required_status_checks gate + non_fast_forward, empty bypass list) once the fast-forward issue is past. Confirmed on Benchmarks runs #27827073571 and #27826231986 (both push:main, step 'Auto-ratchet the perf floor (commit improvements back to main)' -> failure; log: '1 file changed, 2 insertions(+), 2 deletions(-)' then '! [rejected] HEAD -> main (fetch first)' / 'failed to push some refs'). NET EFFECT: (1) the perf-baseline.json floor ratchet NEVER actually lands on main via this path, so the source-of-record floor only ever tightens when a human/orchestrator commits it; (2) the Benchmarks workflow goes RED on every push:main where an improvement was measured (exit 1). UNLIKE bead-autoclose this step is NOT fail-soft. FIX OPTIONS (mirror sq-roe3 resolution): (a) make the push best-effort fail-soft (warn + exit 0) so improvements are opportunistic and the job stays green — but then the floor still never lands without a ruleset bypass; (b) add github-actions bot to the main ruleset bypass list (owner-only, needs:user) AND make the step fetch+rebase main before push to fix the non-fast-forward race; (c) fold the floor ratchet into the periodic .beads/baseline-export PR flow. Recommend: fail-soft NOW (stop the red runs) + bypass-list entry (a+b) as the durable fix, OR PR-based ratchet. [OPUS-4.8] sq-roe3 sibling.
close_reason: Fixed in PR https://github.com/jeswr/sparq/pull/858 — fail-soft + fetch-rebase the bench.yml perf-baseline auto-ratchet push. The main-only commit-back now (1) git fetch origin main && git rebase FETCH_HEAD before the push to survive the non_fast_forward race, and (2) disables errexit around the push, warns + exit 0 on non-zero so Benchmarks is GREEN whether or not the push lands. Measurement + Hard-gate + PR-side perf comparison UNTOUCHED. True floor-landing remains DEFERRED to Option A (github-actions bot on the main ruleset bypass list, owner-only needs:user) or Option C (fold into periodic .beads/data-sync PR sq-2xdg) — fail-soft is the immediate fix. Confirmed on red runs #27827073571/#27826231986. [OPUS-4.8]

Those are gated under sq-qhy4 (external accredited-cryptographer sign-off PENDING; v1 verifier is remediated + internally re-audited only). This bead is ordinary glue unit/integration testing of NON-cryptographic composition logic — frame any docstrings accordingly; do NOT assert any privacy/soundness guarantee (the LIVE privacy-claims CI gate will fail an unqualified claim).
- Standard gate: clippy -D warnings; do NOT lower any coverage floor.
- NOT a floor-raising bead per se (that umbrella is sq-qcnn) — this is a SPECIFIC bounded test deliverable; the floor will rise as a side effect, re-seed via scripts/coverage-gate.py --seed if it does.

title: cargo-vet GATING leg breaks when install-action installs cargo-vet <0.10.2 (can't parse trusted-publisher)
description:
ROOT CAUSE (corrected): the committed supply-chain/imports.lock contains a 'trusted-publisher = github:...' publisher entry (crates.io Trusted Publishing). Parsing that field was added in cargo-vet 0.10.2 ONLY (CHANGELOG #671, 2026-01-12); 0.10.0/0.10.1 reject it with 'missing field user-id for key publisher.wasm-encoder' (the error line number points into cargo-vet's in-memory model, not the on-disk file).

The 'Install cargo-vet' step in .github/workflows/supply-chain.yml used an UNPINNED 'tool: cargo-vet', so the resolved version depended on the taiki-e/install-action build:
 - install-action v2.81.10: no native cargo-vet support -> falls back to cargo-binstall -> installs 0.10.2 -> PASSES.
 - install-action v2.82.0: adds native cargo-vet support pinned to 0.10.0 -> FAILS.
This is exactly why PR #704 (install-action 2.81.10 -> 2.82.0) reproducibly broke the cargo-vet GATING leg, while main (still on v2.81.10) stayed green. It is NOT a transient remote-fetch flake (my first diagnosis was wrong) and the '--frozen' change in #712 does NOT fix it (the parse error is in loading the committed imports.lock, before any network step) — proven by #704's post-#712 run still failing identically with cargo-vet 0.10.0.

FIX (PR #713): pin 'tool: cargo-vet@0.10.2' so the parse version is independent of the install-action default. Bump the pin in lock-step with any new imports.lock schema feature. Once #713 lands, re-run #704's cargo-vet/gate.

Validated: local cargo-vet 0.10.2 'cargo fetch --locked && cargo vet --locked --frozen' on main -> Vetting Succeeded, exit 0. v0.10.2 tag exists on mozilla/cargo-vet; binstall already fetched 0.10.2 in #712's run. [OPUS-4.8]
close_reason: fixed by #713 (cargo-vet@0.10.2 pin), validated by #704 merging green

title: privacy: error-body echo wider than PR-G1 — query-path + RDF-body parse errors echo caller input/loaded-RDF fragments
description:
Audit of cert-privacy (PR #236, epic sq-toze) found the privacy gap register PR-G1 understates the error-body leak surface. PR-G1 claims the UPDATE path (`update failed: {e}`, http.rs:2116) is 'the one exception' and that the leak is 'query text, not loaded RDF data' (→ Low). Independent code read of origin/worktree-agent-af186064192837d69 found additional echo sites:
- http.rs:1812  `bad_request("malformed query: {msg}")` — QUERY parse path echoes the spargebra diagnostic (caller query text). Contradicts the controls.md P-12 claim that query responses 'already use generic bodies'.
- http.rs:2293  `bad_request("malformed RDF body: {e}")` and :2302 `malformed RDF/XML body: {e}` — the GSP write-body load path echoes the RDF parser error (via Graph::load_str → parse_to_triples → e.to_string()), which for a malformed triple can embed a fragment of the LOADED RDF DATA (i.e. actual personal data) — defeating PR-G1's 'not loaded data' severity justification.
- http.rs:2738  `malformed gzip body: {e}`.
Remediation: strip/gate these diagnostics to generic bodies (parity with the query result path) OR put verbose diagnostics behind --verbose; add a regression test asserting default-mode error bodies contain no echoed query/RDF fragment. Pairs with sq-toze.32 (which is a DOC bead, not this code fix). Ref epic sq-toze, PR #236. [OPUS-4.8]
notes:
[OPUS-4.8] SECURITY: error responses leak loaded-RDF fragments to UNAUTHENTICATED callers (B3 no-auth path) — http.rs:2293/:2302, root at sparq-core/src/lib.rs:632 (Graph::load_str e.to_string()). Same root cause as ASVS-G3 error-string hygiene (sq-kfel) — fix together: sanitize/genericize error bodies so no caller input or data content is echoed. Surfaced by the Privacy cert audit (#236).
[OPUS-4.8] COMPLETE echo-site list (sanitize ALL): http.rs:1812 (query text), :2116 (UPDATE), :2293/:2302 (RDF body), :2738 (malformed gzip body), :2860 (exec error), main.rs:875-881 (persist dir.display()), root sparq-core/src/lib.rs:632 (Graph::load_str e.to_string()). Fix = generic error bodies, no caller input/data/path echoed. Pair with sq-kfel (ASVS-G3).
[OPUS-4.8] ASVS-G3 is now tracked as sq-j9zs (the earlier sq-kfel reference was a phantom ID that never persisted). Fix sq-cz89 + sq-j9zs together.
close_reason: Error-body info-leak fixed + merged in PR #241 (HTTP-boundary sanitization, detail→server log, error contract preserved).

title: mmap_corruption_oracle sweeps can OOM-abort the test binary (residual rc=101 source)
description: The corruption sweeps in crates/sparq-core/tests/mmap_corruption_oracle.rs (mmap_loader_survives_corruption_raw/_compressed, quoted_triple_wrong_kind_component_is_safe_not_panic) deliberately feed hostile varint/length bytes to Graph::open. The test's own comment notes an OOM-abort 'cannot be caught and takes the whole process down' — i.e. a corrupt length that drives a huge allocation aborts the WHOLE test binary => exit 101 with no FAILED line, and under llvm-cov no profraw => undercount. This is a SEPARATE potential trigger of the sq-x4jy symptom from the env-var race fixed in ea0ca3e. Mitigations now in place: (1) nextest per-test process isolation + --retries 2 means one aborting test no longer fails the run deterministically and self-heals; (2) sq-znld/sq-ed2i already bound most allocations. Deeper fix if it ever recurs: cap the loader's pre-allocation against the on-disk file length (reject a declared length/count that exceeds the mmap'd file size before allocating), so a hostile length is a clean Err instead of an abort. Found while fixing sq-x4jy.
notes: ROOT CAUSE of the train-blocking coverage flake (sq-x4jy): the mmap_corruption_oracle test feeds hostile lengths/varints to the on-disk-store loader; under llvm-cov instrumentation (extra memory) a hostile length triggers a huge Vec pre-allocation → OOM-abort of the test binary → its profraw is lost → sparq-core coverage drops to ~71% (vs 91%) as a valid-but-low number (and sometimes rc=101). --test-threads=1 + the re-measure backstop did NOT fix it (still failed both passes on #62). The real fix is to CAP the loader's pre-allocation by the actual on-disk file length so a hostile length can't reserve GBs (also a genuine untrusted-input DoS hardening). Fix this and the coverage flake disappears.

title: Flaky sparq-core coverage measurement — intermittently 71% vs 91% (blocks unrelated PRs)
description: The per-commit coverage ratchet intermittently measures sparq-core at ~71% (< floor 78) instead of the true ~91%, failing CI on UNRELATED (even doc-only) PRs (#30, #57). Root cause (flagged by the #29 coverage-gate agent): an llvm-cov test-binary race — a test binary (e.g. the snapshot/mmap-oracle/dict-spill binary) sometimes isn't executed/measured, dropping the %. Fix options: run the coverage test set serially (--no-parallel / --test-threads=1 under llvm-cov), pin/verify the expected test-binary set is measured (fail loudly if a binary is missing rather than silently undercounting), or split the heavy binaries. Until fixed, a re-run clears it (see scripts/coverage.sh). Worst risk: it could also MASK a real coverage regression. Relates to sq-5fd1 (coverage gate) + the #29 hardening.
notes: DIAGNOSED + FIX READY on branch ci-fix-flake-x4jy (commit ea0ca3e). ROOT CAUSE is NOT a snapshot/golden-file test — it is a process-global ENV-VAR data race in UNIT tests: sparq-core dictspill.rs (spill_config_from_env_gate_and_overrides) and sparq-server service_config.rs (3 from_sources tests) called std::env::set_var/remove_var while sibling tests + the production from_env/from_sources paths read std::env concurrently (cargo test = parallel threads). Concurrent setenv/getenv is libc UB (reallocs environ) -> can abort the whole test binary -> 'build+test' exit 101 with no FAILED line AND (under llvm-cov) no profraw -> sparq-core undercount (~71% vs 91%). The pre-existing EnvRestore guards fixed leakage but NOT the concurrent-access race. FIX: made both tests hermetic via injectable env lookups (SpillConfig::from_lookup + ServiceAllowlist::from_sources_with_env; public signatures unchanged); zero set_var/remove_var remain in the workspace. PLUS CI resilience: build+test now uses cargo-nextest --retries 2 (per-test process isolation; 'binary never executed' is deterministic; +cargo test --doc preserves doctests) and coverage.sh retries a per-crate measurement. Validated: env tests 20/20 in a parallel loop; full-workspace nextest 1493 pass/0 fail/28 skip; sparq-core coverage stable 91.28%; clippy -D warnings clean; ci.yml valid+SHA-pinned. This should CLOSE sq-x4jy on merge (root cause removed). Residual SEPARATE rc=101 source (mmap oracle OOM-abort) tracked as sq-f5jh.

title: Reject non-UTF-8 dictionary blob in mmap loader (from_utf8_unchecked soundness hole)
description: Memory-safety soundness hole at the hostile-on-disk-file boundary. Dict::open_mmap (crates/sparq-core/src/dict.rs:1272) validates only dict-meta.bin (magic/version/INLINE_BASE) but performs NO validation of the four data files (dict-terms/offs/hash/hid.bin). MappedDict::stored (dict.rs:567) reads an attacker-controlled u64 offset from dict-offs.bin and slices blob[off..]; rd_str (dict.rs:380) reads an attacker-controlled u32 length then calls std::str::from_utf8_unchecked over those bytes WITHOUT a UTF-8 check -> immediate UB (undefined behaviour) on a hostile/corrupt store whose blob contains non-UTF-8 bytes. A bad offset/length instead panics (DoS). Fix: validate dict-offs.bin length == len*8 and every offset < terms.len() at open time, and replace from_utf8_unchecked with a checked from_utf8 (or validate the whole blob is UTF-8 on load). Complements sq-ky2a (fuzzing). Identified in research/threat-model.md (T-MMAP-UB).

description:
Found + FIXED during sq-6qkq (per-builtin error-path table test), branch test-builtin-errors.

DIVERGENCE (SPARQL 1.1 type-error rule): three string builtins used the lax value_str() coercion (which stringifies IRIs/numbers/booleans like STR()) where the spec requires a STRING LITERAL operand, so a type-error input wrongly produced a VALUE instead of an expression error:
  - STRLEN(<iri>)        returned the IRI's char count (e.g. 11) instead of error  [exec.rs F::StrLen, SPARQL 1.1 §17.4.3.2 — xsd:integer STRLEN(string literal)]
  - ENCODE_FOR_URI(123)  returned simple literal "123" instead of error           [exec.rs F::EncodeForUri, §17.4.3.12 — simple literal ENCODE_FOR_URI(string literal)]
  - LANGMATCHES(123,'en') returned false (a value) instead of error                 [exec.rs F::LangMatches, §17.4.3.15 — xsd:boolean langMatches(simple literal, simple literal)]

FIX: switched those three arms from value_str() to str_lit() (accepts simple/lang-tagged/xsd:string, rejects IRI/number/boolean -> Value::Error). Tagged [OPUS-4.8] in exec.rs. All 144 existing engine lib tests still pass; new builtin_error_paths table test (44 builtins x {valid,type-error,(boundary)}) is green. clippy -D warnings clean. W3C conformance data was not fetched in the worktree so the rdf-tests suite could not be re-run here — FOLLOW-UP: run scripts/fetch-conformance.sh + sparq-conformance to confirm no regression in the fn-* string-function suite.

This bead is the audit record; the fix is on branch test-builtin-errors awaiting orchestrator merge.
close_reason: Resolved: W3C SPARQL conformance re-run after the STRLEN/ENCODE_FOR_URI/LANGMATCHES strictness fix is CLEAN — 1225 pass + 4 divergence = 1229, no regression below the ratchet.

The four open problems (sq-l5og/sq-wvne/sq-tu4e/sq-xc4y under epic sq-pfae) are OPEN beads, not a finished gate.

(i) hidden-issuer set-membership (pk_i in K): BUILT but NOT-yet-sound (sq-z9l; issuer.rs key_set_root/key_membership_witness/hidden_issuer_prover_toml; issuer.nr Poseidon2-Merkle key_set_membership; verifier.rs:3002 bind_hidden_issuer_attestations; gated on sq-qhy4).

(iii) single-use nullifier: ABSENT -> sq-rsd3v.1.

THE GAP this wires: the trust-graph PoC admit() (sq-pfae.10) authenticates the requester WebID IN THE CLEAR, so even with (i)+(ii) presentations are trivially linkable by requester identity. Replace clear-WebID holder binding with in-ZK holder-PoP + nullifier.

HONEST: the WHOLE composite is NOT-yet-sound (the composition seam, sq-qhy4); this is NOT a sound anonymiser today and makes NO privacy claim. title: Delegation-binding challenge: chain-carry + per-request key-proof (invoker==terminal delegate) + nullifier non-replay
description:
Feature 3 (maintainer ask #3) — closes sq-l5og (delegation invocation-binding; admitted delegation is replayable). Structurally the confused-deputy defence of solid-trust-graph-authz-design §4.3.

HONEST SCOPE: ZERO delegation substrate today (verified — no dpop/gnap/zcap/ucan/proof-of-possession across sparq-solid+sparq-server; Session.client is a bare IRI; sparq-prov records prov:wasAssociatedWith single-agent, NOT actedOnBehalfOf; revocation.rs is per-link, no chain-revocation). This BUILDS chain-carry + per-request key-proofing + nullifier non-replay from scratch.

THREE sub-properties as ZK obligations:
1. INVOKER==TERMINAL-DELEGATE: delegation chain = sequence of signed graphs (ZCAP-LD/UCAN) each admitted on the trust rail; terminal delegate key d_n folded into the issuer-signed object exactly as holder-binding folds hpk — NEW domain tag ZKSIG_DG (alongside C1/C2/C3 in crates/sparq-zk/src/sig.rs). Invoker proves possession of d_n's secret via the SAME holder PoK relation (one Baby-JubJub scalar-mul + Poseidon2 digest equality — cheaper than schnorr_verify).
2. KEY-PROVEN: invoker key issuer-attested (predecessor delegate signed d_n into the link), never a free allow-list entry; reuses bind_holder_pok (verifier.rs:3158) over the chain-terminal key.
3. NON-REPLAYABLE: bind to verifier's fresh challenge (audit-#4, field-0 byte-equal) AND single-use via the nullifier (sq-rsd3v.1) so an admitted delegation cannot become a standing graph fact.

EXPLICITLY NOT v1: attenuation (authority subset-of delegator) is host-side monotone, NOT a ZK obligation; confused-deputy in full obj-cap sense NOT prevented (per-request key binding is a PREREQUISITE supplied, not a completed property); deep-chain incremental revocation NOT done (revoked mid-chain link stays live until next re-materialise epoch = UNBOUNDED stale-authority window, unsized); which delegator-permissions snapshot the attenuation intersects is NOT bound. Soundness rides the NOT-yet-sound composition rail (sq-qhy4).

Delegation-replay forgery test (analogue of acp_forged_*_in_acr_document_does_not_grant). research/zk-inference-and-credentials.md §5. [OPUS-4.8]

title: sparq-zk-n3: witnessed-rule-shape derivation_step for N3 {premise}=>{conclusion} rules + builtin gadget whitelist
description:
Feature 2 (maintainer ask #2): prove a SPARQL result over an N3-materialised closure where the dataset ships its own rules. The harder sibling of sq-rsd3v.2 — the rule set is DATASET-SUPPLIED, not a fixed public table. GREENFIELD. Ships AFTER RDFS in-circuit (sq-rsd3v.2) lands and inherits its soundness caveats.

DESIGN:
1. The rule author becomes an ISSUER: commit the N3 rule-graph into the signed-input set K exactly like a TBox (reuse sq-z9l key-set-membership: issuer.rs key_set_root/_sparse, issuer.nr). A derivation is only as sound as its rules; the proof says WHOSE rules.
2. Each N3 rule-firing = a GENERALISED derivation_step whose rule SHAPE is itself a witness (premise/conclusion pattern term-encodings), not a fixed enum tag. Circuit checks: conclusion is the premise pattern under a CONSISTENT variable substitution (encoding-equality over shared variable slots) AND each premise instance is grounded by a hidden committed-graph membership proof or an earlier conclusion.

WITNESS SOURCE (already the right shape): reason_n3_proof / CLI --proof -> ProofStep / n3_proof_tree (crates/sparq-reason/src/lib.rs:18, explain.rs:260); feeds the same ProofTree path as RDFS/OWL.

PROVABLE SUBSET v1 (DECLARE + fail-closed outside it): safe, ground-deriving, builtin-free FORWARD rules {p1 . p2 ...} => {c1 ...} with universals; every conclusion var bound in premise (safety). Whitelisted builtins as fixed gadgets: math: comparisons (greaterThan/lessThan/notGreaterThan/notLessThan/equalTo — REUSE filter_int/filter_signed/decimal verbatim); math: sum/difference/product (field add/mul + range-checks).
EXCLUDED + fail-closed: existentials-in-conclusion (no in-circuit fresh-bnode minting); scoped NAF (log:notIncludes/log:collectAllIn — deferred with completeness sq-rsd3v.6); math:quotient/exponentiation/floats; string:/list:/time: builtins; log:semantics/includes; backward rules not reducible to forward closure; unbounded-closure rules. Path syntax (!/^) OK (sparq-reason desugars before the proof step).

Forge-and-verify test (rule outside subset must be rejected, not approximated). NOT-yet-sound (sq-qhy4). research/zk-inference-and-credentials.md §4. [OPUS-4.8]

title: Structure-aware vectorisation: in-tree KGE trainer that consumes the P0 type-constrained negatives (sq-0wo9e.1 follow-up)
description: DEFERRED REMAINDER of P0 (sq-0wo9e.1, PR #999). sq-0wo9e.1 shipped the two BUILDABLE/additive halves of design §5.A/§2 as reusable primitives in the opt-in `structure` feature: closure-before-vectorise (close_for_vectorise/materialise_closure) + a type-constrained NegativeSampler (Krompass 2015) with an on/off ablation switch. SCOPE FINDING: sparq-vectors has NO KGE training path — embeddings are produced out-of-process (no TransE/ComplEx/RotatE, no triple-scoring, no learning loop), so the trainer that CONSUMES these negatives does not exist in-tree and was deferred (the brief's guardrail: do not build a huge new training subsystem blind; the design #996 may reshape it). This bead tracks: either (a) an out-of-process trainer reference harness that drives the sampler + scores triples + writes the learned vectors back via import_npy, OR (b) a thin in-tree shallow-KGE block — whichever the maintainer chooses on reviewing #996/#999. MUST keep: opt-in/default-OFF, no .spqv format/serving change, the on/off Hits@k ablation gating adoption, no accuracy claim without measured lift. [OPUS-4.8] 🤖 SPARQ agent

title: P6: eval harness (on/off ablation matrix, dataset-gated) + formal-properties test suite
description: FORMAL (6.A, in CI): metamorphic GLOBAL-monotonicity test for the order-preserving encoder (a periodic code FAILS); enum/boolean slot round-trip; 'every closed triple visible to the encoder' assertion; verify-shrinks-to-sound differential; planner-only-safety; metric-correctness guard (non-Euclidean block rejects cosine). EMPIRICAL (6.B, dataset-gated bench, dashboard): per-prior on/off Hits@k+MRR on FB15k-237/WN18RR/YAGO3-10; type-constrained-negatives ablation; numeric block vs LiteralE-style gating baseline; taxonomy distortion Euclidean-vs-hyperbolic-vs-box on the actual subClassOf DAG; grounding multi-hop vs single-hop vs plain-vector RAG; PROFILE-RELATIVE completeness fraction. Record/replay LLM cache for offline CI; fixed seeds.
design: Separates PROVABLE from BENCHMARKED-ONLY. NO numbers baked into markdown (AGENTS.md). Gates every prior's adoption: a prior is adopted only on measured lift. [OPUS-4.8]

title: P5: neuro-symbolic propose(neural)-then-verify(deductive) grounding pipeline (sparq-reason <-> sparq-vectors)
description: Neural side (ANN or LLM) proposes high-recall candidates with NO guarantee; deductive+constraint side VERIFIES: exact engine re-evaluates the BGP (proposed-but-absent triple dropped), SHACL checks datatype/cardinality/enum/unit conformance, closure disjointness+range facts mask provably-wrong candidates. The candidate set can only SHRINK to a sound subset — generalises the existing 'candidates flow into the exact engine' Diverge invariant to SHACL+closure verification.
design: PROVABLE: verify-shrinks-to-sound (any returned exact answer is a real BGP solution; differential test: ANN-proposed set subset-of exact set after verify). BENCHMARKED-ONLY: whether the neural periphery actually raises end-task recall. HONESTY: GraphRAG/KG-RAG does NOT uniformly beat vector RAG — wins multi-hop, ties/loses single-hop; framed as a MEASURED comparison. [OPUS-4.8]

title: P4: flexible minimal-complete grounding selector + verbaliser (subgraph/vector/NL/typed-value)
description: Grounding = fn(query|tool, graph) -> minimal-and-complete OBJECT, modality chosen per request by a dispatcher on the tool's declared output type: (1) SUBGRAPH (smallest connected sub-BGP entailing the answer; exact engine re-evaluates over ANN candidates via vec-predicate+IdMask), (2) typed SUB-VECTOR (relevant blocks only), (3) NL STRING (introspect token-budgeted schema-card + verbalize.rs, extended to render unit-normalised quantities + enum labels), (4) typed VALUE/payload (enum member / unit-typed quantity / boolean directly). Minimality via ABSTAT-style minimal type patterns (Spahiu ESWC 2016) + CS + token/k budgets.
design: Completeness is PROFILE-RELATIVE (materialised RDFS/OWL-RL/N3 closure + DECLARED SHACL shapes) — NOT answer-completeness. Minimality is provable only relative to a stated criterion. Ambiguous NL queries default to subgraph (exact, re-validated). [OPUS-4.8]

title: P3: taxonomy block (Euclidean default; hyperbolic/box ONLY past a measured-distortion gate) + disjointness repulsion/mask
description: Taxonomy sub-vector from rdfs:subClassOf closure (sparq-reason). Euclidean by default; switch to hyperbolic (Nickel-Kiela/Chami) or box (BoxE) ONLY after a measured-distortion gate on the ACTUAL subClassOf DAG beats Euclidean — NOT on a density heuristic. Disjointness (owl:disjointWith/cax-dw in sparq-reason; sh:not in sparq-shacl): train-time margin repulsion + serve-time HARD MASK dropping provably-disjoint candidates. gUFO rigid/role split is OPTIONAL/LAST (annotations rare in the wild).
design: CAVEAT (must-fix): Nickel-Kiela low-distortion is for tree/DAG transitive closures; real rdfs:subClassOf is noisy/multiply-inheriting -> mandatory distortion gate. Disjointness mask is ANSWER-SAFE (removes only provably-wrong neighbours). [OPUS-4.8]

title: P2: enum/datatype/cardinality prior extraction from sparq-shacl + QUDT unit-normalisation
description: Read sh:in/owl:oneOf (codebook block, width=enum size, closed-world), sh:datatype (router confirm), sh:minCount/maxCount + owl:FunctionalProperty (pooling rule: functional->one slot, multi->permutation-invariant pooled block) from sparq-shacl model.rs (no SHACL changes; new reader in opt-in crate). QUDT qudt:unit -> canonical-SI normalise via a bundled table BEFORE the order-preserving magnitude encoder so 1000 m and 1 km share a code; unit mismatch SHACL-detectable.
design: PROVABLE: enum equality is a slot match not a cosine threshold (no recall loss); out-of-enum -> reserved invalid code SHACL rejects. Depends on P1 schema-header+numeric encoder. [OPUS-4.8]

title: RESEARCH (deferred, after the structure-aware-vectorisation research): decentralised vectorisation + minimal-complete grounded-NL conversation over data spread across MANY Solid Pods (e.g. 100)
description:
RAW MAINTAINER REQUEST (2026-06-20): 'Please queue as a future research task, once the current investigation around vectorisation is done; an investigation into how this would be done in a DECENTRALISED context. For instance, how can I efficiently have a conversation over data stored across 100 different Solid Pods?'

SEQUENCING: BLOCKED-ON / starts AFTER the structure-aware-vectorisation research epic (sq-0dksu-family / the epic the deep-research workflow wf_8f0c840f-543 is opening as research/structure-aware-vectorisation.md). ORCHESTRATOR/SWEEP: once that epic exists, wire the explicit bd blocked-by dependency to it.

SCOPE: take the centralised structure-aware vectorisation + flexible minimal-AND-complete grounding + structured/unstructured inference-interplay design and ask how it works when the data is DECENTRALISED across N (e.g. 100) Solid Pods. Key research questions:
- WHERE do the vectors/indexes live: per-pod local index vs a central aggregated index vs a hybrid; who computes embeddings (pod-side vs client-side); privacy of embeddings.
- FEDERATED retrieval: how to get the minimal-AND-complete grounding across 100 pods WITHOUT pulling everything — query routing / source-selection (ties sparq-fedplan select_sources + the MPC seam routing sq-pwr), federated ANN/vector search, top-k merge across pods, early-termination/pruning (FedUP, sq-pwr.3).
- ACCESS-CONTROL + PRIVACY: each pod is independently access-controlled — the retrieval + grounding must respect WAC/ACP + the trust-graph admission (#951/#966) and may want the MPC-over-federated-SPARQL privacy guarantees (sq-pwr); what leaks via cross-pod retrieval.
- FEDERATED STRUCTURED INFERENCE: how the deductive enrichment (sparq-reason closure) composes across pods with heterogeneous/partial ontologies; schema alignment across pods.
- SYSTEMS: latency over 100 sources, freshness/incrementality per pod, caching, the conversation grounding loop (which pods to even consult per turn), cost.
- EVAL: how to assess minimal+complete + clear+concise in the decentralised setting (formal + benchmark; a multi-pod testbed).
RELATES: sparq-fedplan (federated planning), sparq-solid (Solid/WAC/ACP), epic sq-pwr (MPC over federated SPARQL), the trust-graph epic sq-pfae, the security-properties ontology sq-0dksu, sparq-vectors. Deep-research-first per maintainer pattern. [OPUS-4.8]

title: Trust-graph open problem: ZKAPs-grade unlinkable presentation needs a 3-part ZK composite (hidden-issuer + ZK holder-PoP + nullifier); holder-binding to clear WebID is in tension with anonymity
description: OPEN PRIVACY PROBLEM from adversarial review of research/solid-trust-graph-authz-design.md §5. Hiding the issuer is NECESSARY but NOT SUFFICIENT for ZKAPs-grade unlinkability/anonymity. ZKAPs/Privacy Pass give PRESENTATION unlinkability (redemptions mutually unlinkable + unlinkable to issuance, enforced by single-use/rate-limit). But §3.4 REQUIRES holder binding (credentialSubject==Session.agent) which authenticates the requester WebID IN THE CLEAR at the derivation stratum — so even with hidden-issuer + selective-disclosure, the verifier learns WHICH authenticated WebID requests; presentations are trivially linkable by requester identity. THREE pieces needed to genuinely match ZKAPs, current status verified in code: (i) hidden-issuer set-membership = BUILT but NOT-yet-sound/externally-unaudited (sq-z9l: sparq-zk-compose/src/issuer.rs + zk/compose/compose_core/src/issuer.nr + compiled hidden_issuer_d4; gated on sq-qhy4); (ii) hidden-holder ZK proof-of-possession = built+wired with a verifier binding gate bind_holder_pok (sq-i1dt CLOSED 'already implemented on main', verifier.rs:3158, tested in tests/holder_pok_binding.rs) BUT NOT-yet-sound (sq-qhy4) — so it is not a SOUND anonymiser today; (iii) single-use NULLIFIER / rate-limit / double-spend primitive = ABSENT (grep across sparq-zk + sparq-zk-compose finds none). NOTE: the doc previously WRONGLY said hidden-issuer was 'not yet reached' and a reviewer wrongly said bind_holder_pok was 'not implemented' — corrected to BUILT-BUT-UNAUDITED. A ZKAPs-equivalent presentation must replace clear-WebID holder binding with in-ZK holder-PoP + nullifier (membership/possession in ZK + single-use enforcement). Designed/partially-prototyped, NOT shipped or sound. Hard-gated on sq-qhy4. Relates to sq-pfae.8 (P7 privacy). [OPUS-4.8]

title: Trust-graph open problem: conflicting-issuer-fact deny-on-disagreement may be unreachable under input-only stratified NAF; freshness/revocation/issuer-key are not in-reasoner
description: OPEN SEMANTICS PROBLEM from adversarial review of research/solid-trust-graph-authz-design.md §3.3/§3.5. (1) The shipped reasoner permits negation-as-failure ONLY over input-only predicates and rejects NAF over DERIVED predicates (sparq-reason incremental.rs:2130). The §3.5 'conservative deny-on-disagreement' conflict rule needs negation over a DERIVED admitted-fact predicate, so it may NOT be expressible as a monotone stratified-NAF rule in the shipped engine — possibly unreachable, not flagged. (2) FRESHNESS/REVOCATION are NOT in the reasoner today: time is a per-request Rust check (authindex.rs) and any not-revoked guard must be INPUT-stratified (NAF over an input-only predicate) or admission is unsound — the §2.1 diagram implied in-reasoner freshness/revocation. (3) ISSUER-KEY binding is a LIVE forgery vector, not a footnote: with NO DID resolver (P2/sq-pfae.3 unbuilt), trust:issuerKey->verifying-key is an UNVERIFIED binding = silent privilege escalation until P2 ships. (4) The two-unbound-atom seeding caveat was MIS-CITED: it belongs to the INCREMENTAL counting path (incremental.rs:1768); solid uses full reason_n3 which supports math:greaterThan (n3/mod.rs:1245) — so the real termination risk is recursive/unbound-join admission rules over external-graph extents in the FULL evaluator, unanalysed (bound it in P8). RESOLVE: pin which conflict semantics are expressible in the shipped engine vs need an engine extension; specify input-stratified not-revoked/fresh guards; gate issuer-key on P2. [OPUS-4.8]

comments.text:
> 🤖 SPARQ agent (verification + triage lead) — adversarial SOUNDNESS audit of rdf12 triple-term canon (#933 / #960). [OPUS-4.8]

Audited the 5 high/medium SUSPECTED nested-bnode HNDQ issues (position-marker collapse) by EXECUTION against canonicalize_rdf12 / canonicalize_triples_rdf12. RESULT: 0 confirmed, 5 REFUTED. The position-marker collapse the reviewers correctly identified (all triple-term-internal bnodes hashed with Position::Object + outer predicate, no inner subject/object/depth sub-discriminator — rdf12.rs:330-334, 423-444) is a real LOSS OF DISTINGUISHING POWER IN THE HNDQ MARKER, but it does NOT cause a soundness defect, because:

  (M1) Final serialization (rdf12.rs:582-616, relabel_term_canonical) re-renders the ACTUAL Term::Triple structure with c14n labels substituted, recursing through inner subject/object — so distinct inner structure cannot collapse in the output even if two bnodes shared a label.
  (M2) The issuer map itself still separates genuinely-distinct bnodes: HNDQ breaks ties via the descent + each related bnode's first-degree hash (which DOES encode its own local structure), so distinct nodes get distinct c14n labels. Verified directly (anchored inner pair -> 3 distinct labels).

Probes run (all asserted the correct same/different relationship and PASSED):
- symmetric inner swap (automorphism) -> EQUAL (correct)
- asymmetric inner swap (non-iso, distinct leaf predicates) -> DIFFER
- depth-1 vs depth-2 nesting of same bnodes (non-iso) -> DIFFER
- inner-subject vs inner-object bnode, leaf-only (issue 5 exact repro) -> DIFFER
- anchored inner swap (non-iso, no automorphism) -> DIFFER
- self-loop inner-subject vs inner-object pair (non-iso) -> DIFFER
- marker-symmetric inner pair -> input-order/label invariant (deterministic)
- SHA-384 *_with::<Sha384> generic -> rejects triple terms with CanonError::TripleTerm (rdf12 profile is SHA-256 only; there is NO SHA-384 rdf12 variant to mis-canonicalize — boundary confirmed)

Honesty note: one initial probe ("self-referential inner swap") was authored with a WRONG isomorphism premise (I claimed N1~=N2; brute-force enumeration proved them NON-isomorphic and the canon correctly DIFFERENTIATED them). The "failure" was my test, not the canon — corrected to assert NE. No bug.

Bearing on this bead's item (2): the open spec question "should the nested-bnode position marker carry a sub-discriminator?" is a THEORETICAL-COMPLETENESS / spec-cleanliness question, NOT a latent soundness bug in this implementation — empirically the canon is sound on every constructed nested-bnode case. The future upstream draft should frame the sub-discriminator as a robustness/spec-clarity proposal, not a defect remediation. The audit's distinguishing vectors are good candidates for item (4)'s proposed upstream triple-term conformance vectors.

Research-grade estate; ZK side externally-unaudited (sq-qhy4). This is a research finding, not a security guarantee.

title: Implement OWL 2 EL classifier MVP (normalize + CR1-CR5 core completion, single-threaded) in opt-in sparq-reason-el
description:
Phase E1 of the EL track recommended by the OWL 2 EL/QL spike (research/owl2-el-ql-reasoning-spike.md, PR #931, sq-wmeg). Build a MVP OWL 2 EL consequence-based classifier as a NEW opt-in capability crate sparq-reason-el (preferred) or a non-default 'el' feature on sparq-reason — core+wasm zero-cost when off, matching the explain/capability-crate posture.

Scope (MVP, EL+bottom minus RBox): (1) parse an EL/QL TBox from the graph's triples into the four Baader-Brandt-Lutz normal forms (C1 sub D; C1 cap C2 sub D; C1 sub exists r.C2; exists r.C1 sub D) with fresh-name bookkeeping; (2) implement CR1-CR5 saturation over S(C) (subsumer sets) and R(r) (existential links) — CR4 is the load-bearing existential-traversal rule RL lacks; (3) emit the COMPLETE rdfs:subClassOf subsumption lattice as triples into the same dict/Graph seam the RL scm-* rules use (queryable by plain BGP eval), plus owl:Nothing clashes via the existing inconsistencies() shape.

Gate: differential correctness vs ELK (github.com/liveontologies/elk-reasoner, Apache-2.0) on a small EL ontology fixture; clippy -D warnings + tests in BOTH feature states; wire the suite into a feature-matrix.yml leg; G1 new-crate-completeness (README, bench-or-stub, SKILL if public surface). DEFER to later phases: RBox/property-chain + transitive-role saturation (CR10/CR11 -> Phase E2), transitive reduction + scale (E3), concurrency (E4), incremental classification (E5), safe-nominals (CR6) + concrete domains (CR7-CR9). Rust references (small-scale, not ELK-class): whelk-rs, DEALER. [OPUS-4.8]

title: sparq-server: advertise sd:supportedVersion (SPARQL 1.2 SD posture), honesty-gated on engine's actual 1.2 feature state
description:
Issue #917. jeswr verdict: 'Your call on the best thing to do here' (my_call). DECISION TO MAKE in-flight: advertise 1.2 now (SD is a stable-direction WD/ED) vs wait for CR. Recommended call: advertise now BUT strictly honesty-gated, because the SD vocab direction is stable and a 1.2-aware federation client otherwise cannot discover triple-term support; ship it small (est. effort S).

WHAT: In crates/sparq-server/src/descriptors.rs add sd:supportedVersion (and the 1.2 language posture — 1.2 collapses sd:Language to Query/Update and moves versioning to sd:supportedVersion). Today the file advertises ONLY sd:SPARQL11Query (:54) + sd:SPARQL11Update (:56) via sd:supportedLanguage (:344-352); there is no sd:supportedVersion.

HONESTY GATE (load-bearing): only advertise what is genuinely evaluated. NUANCE the proposer missed — there is NO sparql12/rdf12 cargo feature in sparq-engine; SPARQL 1.2 evaluation (triple terms, dir-lang fns) is compiled into the BASE engine, always-on. So unlike federated_query (cfg!(feature="service")) or provenance (Capabilities::provenance), there is no feature flag to key off. Implementer must decide the gate source explicitly: either (a) gate on the engine's documented/conformance-verified 1.2 state (a const/Capabilities field reflecting tested conformance, NOT aspiration), or (b) add an explicit Capabilities::sparql_1_2 field populated from the real build, mirroring http.rs build_capabilities (:2281). Do NOT advertise a blanket '1.2' if only a partial 1.2 subset is conformant — advertise precisely what the conformance suite passes.

OPT-IN: stay inside the existing double-gate (cargo feature `federation-descriptors` + ServerConfig::federation_descriptors flag, both OFF by default). sparq-core/sparq-engine untouched; a build without the feature stays byte-identical. Add a test in the existing pattern (descriptors.rs tests :564+ / tests/federation_descriptors.rs) asserting the version triple is emitted iff the capability is set.

SERIALIZE: sparq-server is a single-writer hot crate — land as ONE PR at a time, AFTER the earlier-queued sparq-server beads (#905, #916). Prior art: SPARQL 1.2 SD ED https://w3c.github.io/sparql-service-description/spec/ . SPARQ-agent self-id; tag [OPUS-4.8].

title: design: SPARQL-callable graph analytics surface for sparq-algos (opt-in) + af-vs-own ontology justification [#914]
description:
jeswr verdict on #914 (greenlight_design, his real-voice comment, NOT the agent): 'Fine with you looking into this if there are no performance degradations. It should also be opt in (as a general rule, it should be possible to build the engine as pure SPARQL without any of the extensions). Can you please do a design and explain why/why not use existing ontologies like `af` vs. building your own.'

DELIVERABLE FIRST = a research/design record, NOT code. The design must: (1) pick the SPARQL surface — property-functions (?x sparq:pagerank ?score, ?a sparq:shortestPath ?b) vs a CALL/table form — built on the EXISTING sparq-engine FunctionRegistry (crates/sparq-engine/src/lib.rs:141, already wired into SHACL-AF), NOT a new mechanism; (2) explicitly argue why/why-not adopt an existing vocabulary, specifically the `af` (Jena ARQ functions) ontology, vs minting sparq's own — and clearly label anything sparq-invented as non-standard; (3) scope the new algorithms to add to sparq-algos (today Rust-API-only: pagerank.rs/centrality.rs/community.rs/graph.rs): weighted edges, shortest path, betweenness/closeness, Louvain/Leiden; (4) cover the blessed model-backed-UDF recipe wiring the existing registry to sparq-vectors (no new trust/crypto surface).

CONSTRAINTS the implementer must NOT lose: (a) OPT-IN — engine must stay buildable as pure SPARQL with the extension OFF; ship as opt-in crate/cargo-feature, default-OFF, gated in BOTH feature states; (b) NO perf degradation — the work-box is NON-canonical, so the no-regression result must be measured on a canonical host before this is armed (do not imply canonical numbers can be produced in-session); (c) design/ontology-justification must be reviewed before any impl bead is opened. No open PR reserves sparq-algos or the engine registry.
close_reason: Design-for-review delivered: research/graph-analytics-sparql-surface-design.md (PR https://github.com/jeswr/sparq/pull/930, auto-merge OFF). Recommends magic property-predicates (text:/vec: rewrite seam) + FunctionRegistry scalars (reject CALL/YIELD); mint http://sparq.dev/algo# rather than squat Jena apf:/afn: (which define zero analytics IRIs). Impl beads in design §8 are blocked-on-design-review; do NOT open them until jeswr signs off on surface + namespace.

title: sparq-canon: non-standard RDFC-1.0 + RDF 1.2 triple-term canonicalization profile (full HNDQ extension, opt-in, clearly-labelled non-standard) — maintainer #913 greenlight
description:
Maintainer @jeswr on #913 GREENLIT implementation (greenlight_impl, real-voice comment, no SPARQ-agent blockquote). DECISION: 'Go for full non-standard profile and implement a non-standard canon.' This OVERRIDES the issue's proposed staging — do NOT ship only the v1 ground-dataset digest; go straight for the full v2 non-standard profile that descends HNDQ (Hash N-Degree Quads) / n-degree hashing into triple-term objects with nested blank nodes. Replace the current fail-closed CanonError::TripleTerm (crates/sparq-canon/src/lib.rs:82-85, message 'RDF 1.2 triple terms cannot be canonicalized (RDFC-1.0 data model)') with the new opt-in profile.

CONSTRAINTS (all from jeswr, do not lose any): (1) CLEARLY LABEL as non-standard — it is not W3C RDFC-1.0; the W3C rdf-canon work is RDF-1.1-only and RDF 1.2 consequences are unsettled upstream (w3c/rdf-star-wg#114). (2) OPT-IN — stays in the standalone sparq-canon member; sparq-core default build + wasm artifact must remain byte-identical; expose behind a distinct feature/profile fn, do not change default canon behaviour. (3) Identify ambiguities in the spec + errors/gaps in the rdf-canon test suite as you go and contribute them UPSTREAM (jeswr's standard practice). (4) Upstream PRs/issues must be marked DRAFT and TAG @jeswr for review BEFORE making them ready for the upstream maintainer. (5) Honesty: sparq-canon is G1 bench-exempt, but the work-box is non-canonical — do not bake perf numbers.

Scope notes from the issue: canonical N-Quads 1.2 token rules for triple terms incl @lang--dir direction; ground (blank-node-free) datasets are well-defined without HNDQ and cover the common credential/VC case; consider optionally constraining triple terms to no-nested-blank-nodes for the common path. Unblocks: sparq-zk commitment/hash pipeline (depends on sparq-canon) for credential-graph shapes, isomorphism compare, digesting. Refs: https://www.w3.org/TR/rdf-canon/ , https://www.w3.org/TR/rdf12-n-quads/ , w3c/rdf-star-wg#114. NOT benchmark-gated; no serialization hotspot.

title: Spike: OWL 2 EL / QL reasoning feasibility (EL consequence-based classifier vs QL query-rewriting) for sparq-reason
description:
jeswr verdict on #912: 'Yes please spike' — greenlight for an EXPLORATORY SPIKE only, NOT an implementation commitment. Deliverable is a feasibility + scoping record (research/ design note), NOT production code yet.

Scope: assess adding, as OPT-IN features alongside the existing OWL-RL forward-chainer, (a) an OWL 2 EL consequence-based classifier (ELK family) computing the complete class hierarchy/subsumption, and/or (b) an OWL 2 QL query-rewriting reasoner (PerfectRef / combined approach) that rewrites a SPARQL query against a QL TBox so plain BGP eval over the unmodified ABox returns certain answers (no materialization). Spike must DECIDE EL-first vs QL-first and the expected dataset/perf target.

Context: Profile enum is {Rdfs, OwlRl} only (crates/sparq-reason/src/lib.rs:25); no classification/subsumption-lattice output and no query-rewriting path exist. research/inference-sota.md already surveys ELK as EXTERNAL SOTA (sparq ships none of it).

CONSTRAINTS (all load-bearing): (1) opt-in crate/feature, core+wasm zero-cost; (2) honest effort is L/XL real algorithms, not rule additions; (3) OWL 2 RL is sound but SILENTLY INCOMPLETE for EL/QL — scm-* rules give partial TBox subsumption, NOT the complete EL procedure; (4) any perf claims (SNOMED ~350k classes in seconds, GO/ChEBI) need CANONICAL numbers and this work-box is NON-CANONICAL — do not bake measured numbers into docs. No EL/QL reasoner exists in Rust, so this would be novel. Refs: https://www.w3.org/TR/owl2-profiles/ , ELK https://github.com/liveontologies/elk-reasoner , Ontop https://ontop-vkg.org/ . Spike output should feed a follow-up impl bead (EL or QL, per the spike's recommendation).

title: Port federated adaptive divergence-triggered re-planner to the LOCAL evaluator (sparq-engine exec.rs), opt-in + benchmark-gated; promote shared policy module only if no degradation in either engine (#903)
description:
Maintainer #903 GREENLIGHT (jeswr, real-voice, 2026-06-19): 'Green light. Run benchmarks to make sure this does improve performance in the main module. Put in a shared module if it doesn't cause degredations in either engine.'

WHAT: Port the existing federated adaptive re-planner from crates/sparq-fedplan/src/adaptive.rs (ReplanPolicy with divergence_factor + improvement_margin hysteresis, AdaptiveExecutor) into the LOCAL evaluator at crates/sparq-engine/src/exec.rs. The local path fully materialises each intermediate join, so TRUE per-stage cardinality is known for free; after each materialised stage, compare actual vs estimated cardinality on the REMAINING BGP and, if a remaining estimate was off by > divergence_factor, re-order the UNEXECUTED patterns (adopt the new suffix order only when it wins by the hysteresis improvement_margin, to avoid thrash). research/optimization-techniques.md flags this as 'near-zero-cost'; currently implemented ONLY in sparq-fedplan, absent from the local join loop in exec.rs.

HARD CONSTRAINTS (do not lose):
1. BENCHMARK GATE — must demonstrate a real perf improvement in the local/main module before landing. HONESTY: the current EC2 work-box is NON-CANONICAL; numbers here are indicative only and cannot be the canonical evidence. Settle the gate on a canonical host.
2. SHARED-MODULE decision is CONDITIONAL: factor the divergence/hysteresis policy into a shared helper so fed + local cannot diverge — but ONLY commit the shared abstraction if benchmarks show NO degradation in EITHER engine (local AND federated). If the shared seam regresses either path, keep per-path implementations.
3. OPT-IN, default OFF: gate behind a new engine cargo feature mirroring sparq-fedplan's `adaptive-replan` (e.g. `adaptive-replan-local`); engine must stay buildable as pure SPARQL with zero adaptive code compiled in when off.
4. RESULT CORRECTNESS: output multiset identical to the static plan irrespective of re-order; port the fed oracle test (adaptive::tests::replan_result_equals_static analogue) into the engine.
5. It is a PORT — reuse the existing policy; no new cost model, no new operators.

SCOPE/NO-EFFECT NOTE: only helps when the initial estimate is wrong AND patterns remain; no effect on single-join or correctly-estimated queries.

Gate before PR: build + clippy + tests in BOTH feature states; update sparq-engine README/SKILL; tag commits [OPUS-4.8]; SPARQ-agent self-id blockquote on the PR.
notes: 🤖 SPARQ agent [OPUS-4.8]: PR https://github.com/jeswr/sparq/pull/948 (auto-merge OFF). Port is CORRECTNESS-COMPLETE: opt-in adaptive-replan-local feature ports fedplan's ReplanPolicy divergence+hysteresis into exec.rs::eval_bgp_binary; result multiset identical to static plan (non-vacuous replan_result_equals_static oracle passes); both feature states green (build+clippy-Dwarnings+tests). Shared sparq-replan-policy crate committed (verbatim policy port; fedplan NOT rewired, its 34 tests untouched/green). HONEST PERF GATE = UNMET: work-box micro-bench (NON-CANONICAL) shows NO win — ~0.93-0.96x (slight regression) when a switch fires, ~1.0x/no degradation when inert. Root cause: the LOCAL planner's per-pattern estimates are EXACT, so it is already well-ordered; the only flippable divergence reorders two MULTIPLICATIVE arms without reducing total materialised work. Bead's HARD benchmark gate not satisfied -> NOT armed on perf; left OPEN for orchestrator/maintainer arming decision (land perf-neutral opt-in vs defer vs redesign vs canonical-host confirm).
close_reason: PORTED + MEASURED (PR #948, CLOSED not merged): the naive fedplan->local adaptive-replanner port is correctness-complete but delivers NO perf win on the local path — the local planner's per-pattern estimates are EXACT (index-range), so GOO is already well-ordered; a divergence-triggered reorder only flips multiplicative arms (can't reduce total work). jeswr's #903 perf precondition unmet => not landed. Negative result captured. Redesign (pruning-aware reorder) tracked separately. [OPUS-4.8]

title: Harden js-sbom lane against external dev-dep additions to a published member (sq-f04e class)
description:
[OPUS-4.8] The JS CycloneDX SBOM lane (scripts/gen-js-sbom.sh + scripts/derive-workspace-member-lock.mjs) is still brittle to NEW EXTERNAL devDependencies being added directly to a PUBLISHED workspace member's package.json (e.g. js/package.json = @jeswr/sparq).

The sq-f04e hardening (#887) only covered workspace LINK deps (link:true nodes pulling in their target closure). It did NOT cover external (registry) dev-deps. PR #922 added test-only dev-deps (@solid/acl-check, @solidlab/policy-engine, n3) to js/package.json devDependencies; derive-workspace-member-lock.mjs projected their full transitive tree (rdflib/undici/cross-fetch/...) into the derived standalone js/ lock, and cyclonedx-npm's internal 'npm ls --omit=dev' then flagged that tree as 'invalid' -> ELSPROBLEMS -> exit 254, GATING the SBOM lane.

WORKAROUND USED in #922: relocated the 3 test-only dev-deps from js/package.json to the repo-root package.json devDependencies (they still resolve for js/test/ via root node_modules hoisting; the runtime --omit=dev SBOM is unchanged — still just fzstd). This keeps the published-package SBOM clean but the lane remains a foot-gun: any future external dev-dep added to a published member re-trips exit 254.

PROPER FIX (defer): make scripts/gen-js-sbom.sh / derive-workspace-member-lock.mjs tolerate external dev-deps under the --omit=dev runtime view WITHOUT weakening what the runtime SBOM reports — i.e. the derived member lock should project the runtime closure cleanly even when the member declares external dev-deps whose transitive tree is dev-only. Add a regression guard (a published member with an external dev-dep must still produce a green SBOM lane). Cross-ref sq-f04e (#887) which hardened only the link-dep case.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #968: js-sbom lane hardened against external dev-deps on a published member — runtime SBOM stays strict (--omit=dev prunes the dev tree), dev SBOM uses cyclonedx --ignore-npm-errors (still enumerates full set) + purl-superset honesty guard, regression test scripts/tests/test_js_sbom_external_devdep.sh wired into gating ci-scripts job. [OPUS-4.8]

title: ZK age-proof Blake3 proof-time breakdown issue (#759) — ~82% gate-count attribution + necessity analysis
description:
Track GitHub issue #759 (https://github.com/jeswr/sparq/issues/759): ZK age-proof proof-time breakdown — what Blake3 hashes (~82% gate-count attribution) and whether it is necessary.

Synthesises three investigations into the hidden-operand numeric FILTER (FILTER(?value >= 18)) age proof:
(1) PROOF-TIME breakdown: GATE counts are the canonical metric (bb gates -s ultra_honk circuit_size; filter_int_d{1..4}=17,416, filter_f64=3,113, reproduces crates/sparq-zk-compose/tests/gate_count_snapshot.json byte-for-byte on nargo 1.0.0-beta.21 / bb 5.0.0-nightly.20260324). Wall-clock is illustrative/non-canonical (EC2 work box). Proving is the dominant Blake3-sensitive phase; witgen+verify are Blake3-flat.
(2) WHAT Blake3 hashes: the canonical N-Triples token of the operand literal (e.g. 48-byte token for xsd:integer 42), one <=64B block = one compression = ~14.3k gates (~82.1%). Host: crates/sparq-zk/src/encode.rs:52-54; circuit re-derivation zk/compose/compose_core/src/filter_int.nr:74-92; h2=Poseidon2 hashes.nr:20-22; truncation field.rs:60-67; binding edge verifier.rs:2078-2087.
(3) NECESSARY? It is the chosen string-canonical binding (constraint A1), replaceable by the numeric value-lane (sq-j506, projected ~3.2k gates) but that RELOCATES canonical-form/binding constraints (A1/A4/B4) across crate boundaries and is GATED on external audit sq-qhy4. #741 (commit c873c459) decision is design-only; impl captured as sq-j506 (numeric lane) + sq-hb75 (issuer scalar-mul).

Design doc: research/zk-age-gatecount-reduction.md (merged #741, commit c873c459).

HONESTY: ZK verifier is NOT externally audited and documented NOT-yet-sound (sq-qhy4/sq-9hrn/sq-1s2). All gate counts/timings are measured circuit/runtime metrics, NOT security guarantees. The 82% figure is a GATE-COUNT attribution (gates track but are NOT identical to wall-clock; work box non-canonical for absolute perf). [OPUS-4.8]
close_reason: Breakdown delivered: GitHub #759 carries the full 3-question analysis (proof-time→gates; what Blake3 hashes = the ~48B N-Triples operand token, ~14.3k gates/~82%; necessity = the A1 string-canonical binding, value-lane alt is sq-j506 audit-gated) + synthesized in research/zk-age-gatecount-reduction.md. #759 left open as the user-facing record.
