It does NOT yet PROVE containment/refinement THROUGH a compound (e.g. an outer odrl:or that subsumes an inner atomic bound, or an odrl:and that refines a dimension). This is a precision (not soundness) gap: every degraded case is honestly Unknown/Possible. Follow-up: extend constraint_implies / permission_subsumes / rule_overlap to reason about and/or/xone operand sets where decidable (an and-window implied by a tighter and-window; an or-set member implying a bound). Keep fail-closed — never report Certain/Contains a compound cannot prove. [OPUS-4.8]

title: JSON-LD compact: pyld strict-third-party faithfulness (@reverse double-invert + non-string @language/@none)
description: 🤖 SPARQ agent [OPUS-4.8]. Discovered while wiring the W3C compact conformance ratchet (sq-3uos5, PR #969). The ratchet's oracle is our OWN oxjsonld self-reparse (reparse(compact(D))==D) — the same oracle toRdf/fromRdf use. It MASKS two pre-existing external-interop boundaries: (a) sparq's @reverse compaction double-inverts (emits the edge as BOTH an @reverse block AND a reverse-mapped forward term, so a strict processor like pyld reads it inverted); (b) a non-string value under a language map's @none member is invalid per spec (language maps hold strings). FIX: more pyld-faithful @reverse compaction (use the reverse term as a forward member, not an @reverse block); route non-string @language-container values to a non-language key. title: JSON-LD compaction: @vocab-relative form over-restricted (rejects ':' '/' '#' in suffix) — suboptimal output
description:
🤖 SPARQ agent — confirmed by adversarial audit of PR #950 (JSON-LD 1.1 Compaction). [OPUS-4.8]

SUBOPTIMAL COMPACTION (low/medium; LOSSLESS — no data loss). The @vocab-relative IRI
compaction is suppressed when the vocab-stripped suffix contains ':', '/' or '#', a
restriction the W3C spec does not impose.

Location: crates/sparq-engine/src/serialize/compact.rs:403
  `&& !rest.contains([':', '/', '#'])`
The spec (IRI Compaction §2.2) only requires the stripped `rest` to be non-empty and not
shadowed by a term definition. The extra character-class check prevents valid vocab-relative
forms (e.g. a predicate whose local part contains a fragment).

REACHABLE ON THE REAL RDF PATH:
  <http://example.org/subject> <http://example.org/ns#value> "test" .
Context: {"@vocab":"http://example.org/","other":"http://example.org/other"}

sparq output: predicate kept as the FULL IRI "http://example.org/ns#value".
pyld (W3C reference): "ns#value":"test".

NOT a losslessness bug: sparq's full-IRI output round-trips through pyld toRdf to exactly
the original triple. This is purely a missed-compaction (output is more verbose than the
spec's canonical compacted form), hence lower priority than the three data-loss beads.

Spec ref: https://www.w3.org/TR/json-ld11-api/#iri-compaction (Step 2.2).

Confirming test (throwaway harness, not committed):
crates/sparq-engine/tests/compact_audit_confirm.rs ::
  s1_vocab_relative_with_fragment_CONFIRMED

Fix sketch: drop the `!rest.contains([':','/','#'])` clause; keep only the non-empty +
not-shadowed checks. Verify against the W3C compact test suite to ensure no over-compaction
(re-expanding `rest` against @vocab must reproduce the IRI).
close_reason: Fixed in PR #963 (https://github.com/jeswr/sparq/pull/963) [OPUS-4.8]: spec-correct compaction + permanent regression test asserting the pyld-verified output and the losslessness round-trip.

title: Add nested-bnode distinguishing-power regression vectors to rdf12 triple-term canon tests (from soundness audit)
description:
> 🤖 SPARQ agent — from the adversarial soundness audit of rdf12 triple-term canon (#933/#960). [OPUS-4.8]

NOT A BUG. The audit (see comment on sq-63g0) confirmed the canon is sound: 0 confirmed / 5 refuted across the high/medium nested-bnode HNDQ suspicions. This is a TEST-COVERAGE improvement only.

The existing crates/sparq-canon/tests/rdf12_triple_term_canon.rs has only ONE non-isomorphic-distinguishing case (nested_bnode_distinguishes_non_isomorphic). The audit constructed several SHARPER distinguishing vectors that exercise the exact HNDQ position-marker-collapse path the aspect reviewers flagged (rdf12.rs:330-334 + 423-444 hash the inner bnodes with Position::Object + outer predicate, no inner subject/object/depth sub-discriminator). All correctly DIFFER. Worth landing as permanent regression tests so any future refactor of hash_n_degree_quads / hash_related_blank_node that DID introduce a false-equal would be caught:

  1. asymmetric inner swap: _:a ex:p <<(_:b ex:q _:c)>> with _:b ex:t1 "x" / _:c ex:t2 "x" vs the inner-swapped form -> must DIFFER (inner subject/object carries the only distinguishing role).
  2. inner-subject vs inner-object leaf bnode: _:a ex:p <<(_:b ex:q "lit")>> vs _:x ex:p <<(ex:s ex:q _:y)>> -> must DIFFER.
  3. depth-1 vs depth-2 nesting of the same bnode set -> must DIFFER.
  4. anchored inner swap (distinct anchor predicates ex:A/ex:B, no automorphism): issuer map must assign 3 distinct c14n labels; output must DIFFER.
  5. self-loop inner-subject vs inner-object pair (non-isomorphic, brute-force-verified) -> must DIFFER.
  6. boundary: canonicalize_quads_with::<sha2::Sha384> on triple-term input -> CanonError::TripleTerm (rdf12 profile is SHA-256 only; assert there is no SHA-384 rdf12 path).

CAUTION for whoever writes these: VERIFY each pair's (non-)isomorphism by brute force before asserting EQ/NE — during the audit one hand-authored pair had a wrong isomorphism premise and produced a spurious "failure" that was a test bug, not a canon bug. Full repros are in the audit comment on sq-63g0.

Relates-to sq-63g0 (item 4 — these double as proposed upstream RDF-1.2 triple-term conformance vectors once upstream semantics are agreed).
close_reason: Landed 6 nested-bnode distinguishing-power regression vectors + brute-force isomorphism oracle in crates/sparq-canon/tests/rdf12_triple_term_canon.rs §5 (sq-mu1cd). From the soundness audit of #933/#960 (sq-63g0): canon confirmed SOUND, these are permanent regression tests. All 5 NE pairs brute-force-proven non-isomorphic before asserting NE; vector 6 boundary (SHA-384 standard path rejects triple terms) confirmed. Gates green both feature states. [OPUS-4.8]

title: CI hardening: clippy gate misses default-OFF feature-gated code (workspace clippy runs without --all-features) — feature-gated lints slip the aggregate gate
description:
DISCOVERED 2026-06-20 during the #936 (sq-jluc) clippy-gate fix. The CI `lint` job's `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` runs WITHOUT `--all-features`, so clippy lints inside default-OFF feature-gated code (e.g. `#[cfg(feature="result-cache")]` modules) are NEVER checked by the aggregate `gate` — they only surface via the per-crate `feature-matrix.yml` legs (which run tests, and per-crate clippy for some features) OR via the bundled `cargo doc --all-features` rustdoc step (which is what actually caught #936's broken intra-doc links, and earlier #926's). 

CONSEQUENCE: a clippy lint (not just a rustdoc link) inside a default-OFF feature module could slip the main gate and only be caught — if at all — by a feature-matrix leg that happens to enable that feature. Two real PRs (#926, #936) hit the rustdoc half of this class.

PROPOSED FIX (CI hardening): either (a) add a workspace `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` step to the gating lint job (cost: longer lint job, possible feature-unification interactions — verify it's sound under unification first), OR (b) ensure every opt-in feature has a feature-matrix leg that runs `clippy -D warnings` (not just tests) for that feature, and make that gating. Decide (a) vs (b) by cost. Relates to the recurring rustdoc-`--all-features` link breakage class. [OPUS-4.8]
notes: AGENT-DEFINITION PREVENTION HALF DONE — PR #955 (opus/rustdoc-allfeat-gate, [OPUS-4.8]). Added the verbatim 'cargo doc --workspace --no-deps --all-features' / RUSTDOCFLAGS=-D warnings step to the MANDATORY pre-PR gate checklists of .claude/agents/sparq-rust-feature.md (Your gates, next to clippy -D warnings) AND .claude/agents/sparq-merge-fixer.md (Gates after resolving) — the sibling of sq-t7oe's readme-template addition — plus a one-line note + cross-link in AGENTS.md's Post-batch re-evaluation base-gate prose that the gating clippy (gate) lane ALSO runs cargo doc --all-features -D warnings. So feature-gated rustdoc private/broken-intra-doc-link breakage (the #926/#936/#950/#954 class) is now caught IN-WORKTREE before the PR opens. STILL OPEN on this bead: the CI-side hardening half — add 'cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings' to the gating lint job (option a) OR make every opt-in feature's feature-matrix leg run gating clippy -D warnings (option b); decide by cost. [OPUS-4.8]

title: sparq-vectors: persist the delta sidecar to disk (durable add/remove/update across process restarts)
description: Follow-up to sq-pi44 (PR #880), which landed the IN-RAM delta sidecar (add/remove/update against a finalized .spqv base + compact, opt-in `delta` feature). The delta is currently lost when the VectorStore handle is dropped — `compact` is the only durability path. Add a PERSISTED on-disk delta sidecar (its own little-endian format alongside the .spqv, e.g. .spqd) so incremental mutations survive a process restart without a compact: an append section (id+vector pairs) + a tombstone section + a header carrying the base graph fingerprint (the sq-32i5 generation tie) so a persisted delta is validated/rejected against a mismatched base on open. Open should load base mmap + replay/mmap the delta; design for crash-durability (fsync discipline, partial-write detection) like the StreamingWriter sidecar. Reuse the in-RAM VectorDelta as the in-memory representation. Keep it additive under the existing `delta` feature; result-equivalence test: open(base + persisted-delta) == the in-RAM (base + delta) view == compact().
close_reason: Persisted on-disk .spqd delta sidecar landed in PR https://github.com/jeswr/sparq/pull/926 — crash-durable save_delta (tmp+fsync+rename) + open_with_delta replay, base-fingerprint generation tie, partial-write detection. Result-equivalence open(base+persisted)==in-RAM==compact() tested. Opt-in delta feature, no new dep.

title: Document the .spqv/.spqg id-keyed staleness contract: query persisted stores via Graph::open, never a re-parsed-from-RDF graph (sq-xhiv sound remedy)
description:
sq-xhiv asked to make the sparq-vectors graph fingerprint dict-id-order-independent so a graph re-loaded from RDF at a different RAYON_NUM_THREADS does not 'spuriously' fail check_against. That was closed won't-fix-as-specified: the .spqv VectorStore / .spqg DiskAnnIndex are keyed by RAW dictionary term id, so an order-independent fingerprint would make check_against PASS a genuinely-mismatched (id-shifted) re-loaded graph and the subsequent query would serve WRONG vectors (measured). The re-load 'mismatch' is therefore NOT spurious — it is a correct fail-closed rejection.

The SOUND, in-scope remedy is documentation + a usage-discipline guard, NOT a fingerprint change:
1. crates/sparq-vectors/src/fingerprint.rs + store.rs + diskann.rs module docs: state explicitly that an id-keyed store/index is valid ONLY against the EXACT graph generation it was built against; to serve it, REOPEN the persisted graph (Graph::open, which mmaps the frozen dict id order), do NOT re-parse the source RDF (the parallel sharded merge assigns thread-count-dependent ids, so a re-parse yields a different id->term binding and check_against will correctly reject it).
2. Consider a doc-test / example showing the persisted round-trip (save -> open -> query OK) vs the re-parse trap (load_str -> query -> descriptive fail-closed error).
3. OPTIONAL larger follow-up (separate bead if pursued): make the store/index/mask TERM-keyed (re-resolve neighbours via term, not raw id) so a logically-identical graph at any thread count is queryable. That changes the on-disk format + the mask_cache key and is a real redesign, not a one-PR change. [OPUS-4.8] sq-xhiv follow-up.

title: Stabilise large-result ORDER BY tie order (parallel par_sort_by is not stable)
description: Orthogonal finding from audit sq-xom2. crates/sparq-engine/src/exec.rs::order_bindings returns Ordering::Equal for ORDER BY ties with no secondary tie-break. Serial path uses stable sort_by (ties keep input order); the >=PAR_THRESHOLD parallel path uses par_sort_by which is NOT stable, so tie order is non-deterministic EVEN AT A FIXED THREAD COUNT (separate cause from dict-ids). Spec-optional (SPARQL leaves ORDER BY tie order unspecified) and rarely bites conformance (W3C ORDER BY tests are authored without ambiguous ties), but it makes any internal golden over a tied ORDER BY result flaky. Fix: deterministic secondary tie-break key OR a stable parallel sort. See research/dict-id-order-determinism-audit.md. [OPUS-4.8] sq-xom2 follow-up.
close_reason: CLOSED as not-an-issue: premise factually wrong. The bead asserts the parallel ORDER BY path (par_sort_by) is non-stable so ties are non-deterministic even at a fixed thread count. But rayon's par_sort_by IS a stable parallel merge sort (rustdoc: 'stable, does not reorder equal elements'); the unstable entry point is par_sort_unstable_by, which order_bindings does NOT use and never has (par_sort_by since commit 1ebbf32a). So the parallel path preserves tied rows' b.rows input order exactly like the serial sort_by -- tie order is ALREADY deterministic at a fixed thread count. The only cross-thread variation is the dict-id order of b.rows itself (umbrella property, covered by sq-8qzz/sq-b83e). No total-order tie-breaker added: would cost a term materialisation per tied row for an order SPARQL leaves unspecified. Code comment + audit correction landed in PR #716.

title: Golden/snapshot determinism guard: serialised RDF + unordered/tied results must canonicalise or pin RAYON_NUM_THREADS
description: From audit sq-xom2 (research/dict-id-order-determinism-audit.md). sparq-core dict-id assignment is thread-count-dependent (default_shards = (rayon::current_num_threads()*2).clamp(4,64)), and it surfaces in OBSERVABLE-but-spec-unspecified order: RDF serialisation row order (serialize.rs writers emit graph_triples()=iter_ids()=SPO-index=dict-id order, no canonical sort), SELECT row order without ORDER BY, CONSTRUCT/DESCRIBE order, ORDER BY tie order. None is pinned canonically TODAY (conformance uses bag/multiset comparison; existing snapshot/differential tests sort by term first), so this is a LATENT footgun, not a present bug — but it is exactly what made the #691 label_propagation test host-flaky. Add a lightweight test-helper + CONTRIBUTOR note (and a cheap CI lint if feasible) so any new test pinning serialised RDF or an unordered/tied result either sorts by term or sets RAYON_NUM_THREADS. [OPUS-4.8] sq-xom2 follow-up.

title: Audit: does any OBSERVABLE/canonical output depend on sparq-core's thread-count-dependent dict-id assignment order (parallel sharded merge)?
description: Surfaced by the #691 (sq-lqty) fix: sparq-core's parallel sharded dict merge (default 'parallel' feature) assigns dictionary ids in a THREAD-COUNT-dependent order (reproduced: RAYON_NUM_THREADS=2/4 vs 1/3/8/16 give different id orders). This leaked into sparq-algos NodeGraph node-index assignment (now fixed via canonical-term ordering in graph.rs). QUESTION: does anything ELSE that is observable/canonical (serialization order, result iteration order without ORDER BY, any snapshot/hash, bench determinism) depend on that internal dict-id order? Likely fine (dict-ids are internal; N-Triples output + result sets are separately canonicalized), but worth a scoped audit. If a real leak is found, bead the fix; if none, close with the evidence.
close_reason: AUDIT COMPLETE. Conclusion in research/dict-id-order-determinism-audit.md (PR pending). VERDICT: NO leak into any REQUIRED-canonical surface — RDF canonicalisation (sparq-canon), ZK graph->leaves commitment encoding (sparq-zk), HDT write (sparq-hdt), and the W3C conformance comparator all canonicalise/sort on the LEXICAL term form, independent of dict-id order; conformance compares unordered results as a bag (sequence only for ORDER BY). The dict-id order IS genuinely thread-count-dependent (default_shards = (rayon::current_num_threads()*2).clamp(4,64)) and DOES surface in OBSERVABLE-but-spec-UNSPECIFIED places (RDF serialisation row order via serialize.rs graph_triples=iter_ids=SPO-index order; SELECT row order w/o ORDER BY; CONSTRUCT/DESCRIBE order; ORDER BY tie order) — none pinned canonically today, so latent footgun not present bug. ONE real robustness sharp edge: sparq-vectors fingerprint content_hash is id-ordered BY DESIGN; safe on persisted-store path (save_mmap freezes ids), can spuriously mismatch if a store is bound to a graph RE-LOADED from RDF at a different thread count (fails CLOSED). Follow-up beads: sq-xhiv (P2 fingerprint fix), sq-8qzz (P3 golden-determinism guard), sq-8m65 (P3 ORDER BY tie stability), sq-b83e (P4 doc reword). Also corrected a sub-investigation's claim that the sharded merge makes dict-ids thread-count-INDEPENDENT — it does not (deterministic only at a fixed shard count). [OPUS-4.8]

title: sparq-mpc: scrub the ChaCha20 key schedule in SecureRng (upstream rand_chacha zeroize, or roll-our-own ZeroizeOnDrop ChaCha wrapper)
description:
Follow-up to sq-19ej (the seed buffer + cached keystream block are now scrubbed; this is the residual). [OPUS-4.8]

The inner rand_chacha::ChaCha20Rng key schedule (the expanded ChaCha key, recoverable via get_seed()) cannot be zeroized in place from sparq-mpc: rand_chacha exposes NO zeroize feature and no Drop/Zeroize impl and no &mut accessor to the private key words. RE-VERIFIED at the latest published rand_chacha 0.10.0 (released 2026-02-02) as well as the pinned 0.9.0 — neither has a zeroize feature (features are just default/std/serde[/os_rng]). The value is stack-allocated so there is no heap allocation to zero and overwriting the binding does not scrub prior stack bytes.

Options to fully close:
1. Upstream PR to rust-random/rand adding a 'zeroize' feature + ZeroizeOnDrop for ChaCha*Rng (preferred; benefits the ecosystem). Track the rand issue/PR.
2. Roll-our-own minimal ChaCha20 CSPRNG wrapper that sparq fully owns and can #[derive(ZeroizeOnDrop)] on the key/counter state. Heavier; only if upstream stalls.

Exposure is LOW: SecureRng is session-lived (one dealing session), never persists a long-term secret, is Debug-redacted and !Clone. Documented honestly in crates/sparq-mpc/src/rng.rs and compliance/cryptoreview/gap-register.md CR-G5. Relates to sq-8xug (rand-ecosystem 0.10 upgrade) — the upgrade does NOT itself add zeroize, but is the natural point to re-check upstream. Mark for Fable crypto re-review.

title: [cert][gap ASVS-G4] No explicit SPARQL parse-depth bound — deep-nesting DoS relies on spargebra recursion + body cap (ASVS V5.5.2)
description: ASVS V5.5.2 (recursive/deeply-nested input resistance). SPARQL parsing uses vendored spargebra recursive descent (crates/sparq-engine/src/lib.rs:379); deep nesting is bounded only by --max-body-bytes (1 MiB default), not by an explicit parse-depth constant. SHACL has explicit cycle/recursion guards (sparq-shacl path.rs/eval.rs) but the SPARQL path does not. Risk: a pathological 1 MiB query of deeply nested groups/expressions could deep-recurse the parser (stack). Remediation: add a fuzz assertion / corpus entry for deeply-nested SPARQL (parse_sparql target already exists) confirming no stack overflow at the body cap, OR add an explicit nesting-depth guard. Ref sq-toze / sq-toze.10. [OPUS-4.8]

MINOR severity: orchestrators (k8s) typically use their own liveness/readiness probes against /health and ignore the image HEALTHCHECK, and bare 'docker run' health is a nice-to-have. title: bench: HDT suite — load-and-decode triple-count gate + load_s/ratio advisory + hdt-cpp competitor (decode-only, query-over-HDT NON-goal)
description:
Design: capability-benchmark-program.md §3.7. Workload: fixed .hdt archive (vendored snikmeta.hdt for correctness; synthetic ~1M-triple archive via bench_load for perf). Compare LOAD-AND-DECODE-TO-NATIVE + triple-pattern resolution on the SAME archive.
DETERMINISTIC gate (mode:auto): triple count of the loaded graph (round-trip already asserts snikmeta.hdt -> 328 triples) + decoded term-set equality (roundtrip.rs/write_roundtrip.rs). Optionally bytes-on-disk of a save-produced archive once the in-memory encoder bead sq-ashy lands (until then write goes through temp-NT round-trip -> encode-perf parity is an explicit non-goal). TIMING advisory: hdt_load_s, hdt_vs_ntgz_load_s (a ratio — survives box contention).
Competitors: hdt-cpp + hdt-java (rdfhdt refs; core LGPL / tools Apache; rdfhdt/hdt-cpp docker exists; rdf2hdt/hdt2rdf/hdtSearch). Fair = load + memory + TP resolution on the same .hdt, matching mapped (mmap) vs loaded (in-RAM) regimes. CRITICAL CAVEAT: sparq-hdt DECODES HDT into sparq's own Dict/Graph (HDT as ingest format) then queries its own indexes; hdt-cpp/java query compressed BitmapTriples in place (HDT as queryable store). So load-and-decode-to-native is the ONLY like-for-like; query-over-HDT head-to-head is NOT — gate/compare load+decode only. Adapter report-cli/docker, behind the hdt cargo feature.

MPC: tighten oblivious shuffle to the AS-Waksman optimal switch count (-1 switch/level)
description: crates/sparq-mpc/src/oblivious.rs builds the plain Benes/Waksman recursive network (floor(m/2) input + floor(m/2) output switches per level). The AS-Waksman redundancy-removal optimization fixes the first output pair (no switch) to shave one switch per recursion level -> ~n fewer conditional swaps overall, the optimal arbitrary-size count ~n*ceil(log2 n)-n+1. We deferred it because the naive fixed-pair pinning over-constrains the routing for ODD m (output 1 pinned BOTTOM clashes with the odd-trailing input pinned TOP); the correct AS-Waksman routing seeds the alternating path so the fixed pair is a consequence, not an axiom. Perf-only: the plain form is already O(n log n) and routes/has-full-support for all permutations (tested to n=9). Verify any change still reaches all n! perms (the anti-Benes-bias property) and routes every permutation (brute-force to n=7). [OPUS-4.8] From sq-18lk.

title: sparq-core: chunk-parallel TriG IN-MEMORY loader (reuse turtle_chunks statement chunking)

TriG is the deferred half: it is NOT line-oriented (it nests GRAPH g { ... } / { ... } blocks carrying Turtle's @prefix/@base scope and document-scoped blank-node labels), so byte-range newline chunking is wrong. The tractable approach is to reuse the existing turtle_chunks statement-terminator chunking (prefix-snapshot broadcast + interspersed-directive replay) extended to (a) track the enclosing GRAPH block as routing context per statement and (b) handle the block-open/close + the 'g {' / 'GRAPH g {' headers as units, then run the per-graph sharded-dict merge already factored out as merge_partials(). Gate on the parallel feature, keep the serial fallback, and add a differential test (chunked == load_dataset_serial, byte-identical: default + named graphs, bnodes across chunks, multiple/blank-node-named graphs) mirroring parallel_nquads_matches_serial. Distinct from the out-of-core quad build. Risk: blank-node + prefix scope across GRAPH blocks and chunk boundaries — correctness is paramount, fall back to serial on any mis-split.

title: MPC: multi-secret / batched share_private_input (per-row hidden values, vectors, per-graph commitments)
description: share_private_input extracts exactly ONE integer per holder (extract_single_integer, single-row/single-column), so per-row hidden values, salary vectors, or per-graph commitments cannot be secret-shared — capping secure computation to one scalar per party. Generalise to batched/vector secret sharing (Vec<Fp> per holder with a documented row-binding) so the secure aggregate and hidden-value join can range over more than one value per source. Prerequisite to any realistic multi-row hidden federated query. Gap raised in the area but not in its proposed-bead list; surfaced here so it is not lost.

title: MPC: federation-level OWA / omission negative tests (a dropped holder/graph/credential must not forge a valid result)
description: Architecture conventions #8 and §4.2 require endpoint-independent OWA-safe semantics: omitting credentials must not forge a valid result, and a short-count/dropped-graph view must be detectable (the issuer-signed true-triple-count + salt in §4.3 step 1 is the intended defence). The crate has holder-level and join-soundness tests but NO federation-level negative test that a holder dropping a graph, returning a truncated partial, or omitting a contributor either cannot fabricate a passing result or is surfaced as a detectable discrepancy. These tests also document honestly which omissions are NOT yet detectable pre-M4 (no signed count binding yet). Acceptance: dropped-holder / truncated-partial / omitted-row negative tests each asserting the actual behaviour.

title: MPC: oblivious hidden-value join must hide the bipartite MATCH STRUCTURE, not just the payload multiset (privacy spike, distinct from the perf bead)
description: HiddenValueJoin opens m=d*r for every (i,j) pair, so whoever drives the opens learns the full bipartite match pattern (which left row matched which right row), even though the output multiset is canonicalised. True circuit-PSI/oblivious join reveals only the match COUNT or the joined multiset, never positional structure. This is a PRIVACY property orthogonal to the O(|L|*|R|) PERF concern already filed (sq-t21/sq-h99, both confirmed DEFERRED): the cuckoo-bin opt could be built without fixing the positional leak and vice versa. Spike: characterise exactly what the all-pairs open leaks to each party, state it in the join doc, scope the oblivious-shuffle/shuffled-open mitigation, and pin the current leakage with a test before any fix.

title: MPC: collision-resistant Term->Fp key encoding + injectivity contract for HiddenValueJoin
description: HiddenValueJoin takes the private join key as a pre-encoded Fp and the struct doc admits the encoding is the holder's untested responsibility (tests use a hand-injective small-int map). For real RDF Terms, secret-shared field equality is a SOUND stand-in for term equality only if the encoding is injective on the join domain (a collision = a false match = a soundness break the differential tests can't see because they avoid collisions by construction). Provide a documented Term->Fp encoder (domain-separated hash into Fp, stating the 2^61-1 birthday bound) + a collision-detection path or explicit assumption + near-collision test. The on-ramp the M4 in-circuit encoding-correctness proof will later constrain.

title: ZK: extend filter coverage — negative xsd:integer + xsd:decimal + general xsd:double (currently fail-closed/unprovable)
description: filter_int.nr handles only canonical non-negative integers (D<=19, no sign); negative integers, xsd:decimal, and the general fractional/scientific/rounded double fragment are all rejected fail-closed. Sound but narrow — bounds which real credential FILTER queries can be proven (negative coordinates, decimal amounts). Add a signed-integer + a decimal/IEEE-parse circuit member with an in-circuit decimal->IEEE round-to-nearest-even path; measure gates with `bb gates` first per noir-optimisation.

title: ZK: bind HolderPoP to a SPECIFIC credential (issuer-attested holder<->credential binding)
description: bind_holder_pop proves possession of a holder key trusted by an external registry but NOT that the key is bound to the presented credential (README/verifier doc: deferred). A trusted holder can therefore present a credential issued to a DIFFERENT holder. Have the issuer attest a holder-key binding (extend sparq_zk::sig signed object) and the verifier require the PoP key match the credential's attested holder, closing the sender-constraint gap.
close_reason: already implemented on main (sq-z8s7 B1): crates/sparq-zk-compose/src/verifier.rs fn bind_holder_binding step (4) (line ~4263) requires the presented PoP key's digest == the issuer-attested holder_pk_digest, and verify_holder_attestation_signature anchors that digest in the issuer's ZKSIG_C4 commitment_message_with_holder signature under the external trusted K — closing the 'trusted holder A presents holder B's credential' sender-constraint gap. CheckError::HolderKeyMismatch fail-closed; tested via holder binding suites.

title: ZK: in-circuit entailment-closure proof — prove an UNDISCLOSED antecedent is in the committed graph's RDFS/OWL closure
description: sq-314 enforces derivation_steps but only grounds them over the DISCLOSED base (verifier.rs doc 'deferred: in-circuit closure proof'). So an entailed claim must disclose every antecedent, defeating privacy for inference-bearing presentations (the §5 inference goal). title: sparq-hdt: direct in-memory PFC + BitmapTriples encoder for HDT write (skip the temp N-Triples round-trip)

title: MPC: equality/mult open only DETECTS, never CORRECTS, under the honest-majority party count
description: Discovered during WI-2 (sq-7q9i). The degree-2t equality/mult open now routes through the RS checker (reconstruct_degree -> reconstruct_robust at degree 2t), but the honest-majority constructor fixes t=floor((n-1)/2), so for a degree-2t product: odd n gives n=2t+1 (ZERO redundancy -> no detection, needs a MAC = WI-4/sq-6d6g); even n gives exactly one redundant share (e_max = floor((n-2t-1)/2) = 0 -> DETECT-and-abort only). Robust CORRECTION at degree 2t (e_max>=1) needs n>=2t+3, which the constructor NEVER provisions for the equality primitive. So in practice secure_equal can at best detect-and-abort (even n), never auto-correct a cheater. The reconstruct_degree correction arm IS exercised by a property test that builds a degree-2t sharing directly with n>=2t+3, but no production path reaches it. Follow-up options: (a) allow the equality test to open its degree-2t product over an OVER-PROVISIONED party set (n>=2t+3) when robustness (not just abort) is wanted; (b) reduce the product degree back to t via a BGW/DN degree-reduction round before opening, so the open is degree-t with the full degree-t correction budget; (c) leave detect-and-abort as the honest envelope and document it. Decide + implement/document. Files: crates/sparq-mpc/src/shamir.rs (reconstruct_degree doc), join.rs (secure_equal), adversarial_tests.rs (degree_2t_open_* props).

title: MPC: sharpen cheater attribution in robust reconstruction (sound detection, heuristic blame)

When BW correction SUCCEEDS the recovered Q does pin the true cheaters (disagreeing_points vs Q is exact); we could surface that even on the success path (currently only the secret is returned). Follow-ups: (1) on successful correction, optionally return the corrected-share indices as identified cheaters; (2) for the abort path, try multiple reference subsets / a voting scheme to improve blame; (3) document the residual RS-miscorrection window (>e coordinated errors landing within distance e of another codeword) — astronomically unlikely for random Fp=2^61 deltas but a real adversarial caveat. title: sparq-solid: precise variable-GRAPH write check under USING/WITH (currently conservative fallback)
description: sq-biss made GRAPH ?var write-permission checks precise by evaluating the WHERE over the full store and checking write only on the concrete bound graphs. But a DELETE/INSERT...WHERE carrying a USING/WITH clause falls back to the conservative all-graphs check, because the apply's Dataset::build_using re-scope semantics (named:None keeps ALL store named graphs, the parser's encoding of WITH) cannot be faithfully reproduced by a plain SELECT whose FROM/FROM NAMED dataset (build_active) treats named:None as the EMPTY named set — a serialized query would under-count the GRAPH ?g bindings and risk a hole. To make USING/WITH precise too, sparq-solid would need to evaluate the binding-enumeration SELECT against the same active dataset the engine's update path builds (build_using), which is currently private to sparq-engine's update module. Options: (a) expose a pub build_using/active-dataset helper from sparq-engine; (b) translate the QueryDataset into an explicit FROM NAMED list of the kept store named graphs before serializing. title: External (sharded/dict-spill) N-Triples build does not support RDF 1.2 triple terms
description: The disk-spilling external N-Triples builders (build_external_ntriples_sharded via ShardedDict::intern_partials, and build_external_ntriples_dictspill via SpillInterner::intern_batch) consolidate partial dicts through a HASH-SHARDED interner that cannot represent RDF 1.2 triple terms (<<( s p o )>>): a triple term's components are hash-routed to a shard AND referenced structurally by the triple, breaking the term<->id bijection across shards (the in-shard interners assert/panic on Term::Triple). sq-hxgb taught the byte parser (nt::parse_chunk) to ACCEPT triple-term objects, and the IN-MEMORY parallel loader (parse_ntriples_parallel) now falls back to the serial merge_remap when any partial contains one. The SERIAL external path (build_external_ntriples_parallel / merge_remap, sharded=false) also handles them. But the SHARDED and DICT-SPILL external paths now return a CLEAR ERROR (reject_triple_terms_in_external_build in lib.rs) instead of panicking/corrupting. FIX: give the sharded/spill consolidation a real triple-term path (e.g. route triple-term components to their shards first, then intern the triple referencing the resolved shard ids in a second pass; or fall the affected batch back to serial merge). Until then, Graph::build_external on triple-term N-Triples must use the serial path (SPARQ_SHARDED_DICT=0) or load in memory. Found by sq-hxgb (Opus 4.8).

title: update_in_place is non-atomic on multi-op request failure (no engine-level rollback)
description: FINDING (sq-qu8o, contract tests in crates/sparq-engine/src/update.rs mod update_contract): a SPARQL UPDATE *request* is a ;-separated op sequence and per SPARQL 1.1 should be all-or-nothing, but the engine's delta-overlay entry point update_in_place(&mut Graph, sparql) applies ops in place and, on op K failing, leaves ops 0..K-1 committed (a partial prefix) — verified by test in_place_request_is_partial_on_error_by_contract. This is currently DOCUMENTED-and-relied-upon (sparq_serve::ApplyUpdates::apply contract; the serve writer recovers atomicity via fork -> apply -> seal-only-on-Ok), so the PRODUCTION HTTP path IS request-atomic. The rebuild path update() is atomic by construction (rebuild_request_is_atomic). The gap: any direct library consumer of update_in_place gets silent partial application on error — a footgun. Options: (a) add an atomic update_in_place wrapper (fork+seal internally) as the public default; (b) document the non-atomicity on update_in_place's rustdoc + steer callers to update() or the fork pattern; (c) leave as-is (serve is the only first-party caller). Low priority: no production-path bug, fully test-pinned. NOT a SILENT-contract bug — CLEAR/DROP/CREATE auto-create no-op success is spec-conformant (SHOULD, not MUST, conditioned on recording empty graphs).

title: Core: cheap O(overlay) Graph::snapshot API (Arc-shared immutable base)
description: Add a cheap Graph snapshot that shares the immutable base (perms + compacted dict arena) behind Arcs so snapshots are O(overlay), not O(triples). Unblocks the server double-buffer collapse, Python Graph.copy(), and the RSP overlay-snapshot EvalMode. Structural change across every storage mode (incl. mmap + compressed). Design in the design field. (was the workspace TODO.md cheap-snapshot rationale — now beaded + doc deleted)
design:
Cheap O(overlay) Graph snapshot API — the core structural change that unblocks the
server double-buffer collapse (sq-dfs), Python Graph.copy() (sq-6h8), and the RSP
overlay-snapshot EvalMode (sq-j39). (Design preserved from the deleted workspace TODO.md.)

PROBLEM. `Graph` is not (and should not be naively) `Clone`: a deep copy of the
dictionary arena and the six permutation indexes is O(n). The server's SPARQL Update
path (crates/sparq-server/src/http.rs::Writer) currently gets microsecond steady-state
updates WITHOUT core changes by double-buffering — two physical Graphs alternate between
*published* and *spare* — but that pays ~2x graph residency, a one-time O(graph) rebuild
on the first update (and again after a failed update discards a buffer), and a
spare-reclaim wait/rebuild when a reader holds a snapshot past the query budget.

PROPOSED API.
  - `Graph::snapshot(&self) -> GraphSnapshot` (or make `Graph` a cheap `Clone`): an O(1)
    copy that SHARES the immutable base — `TripleStore::perms` and the compacted dictionary
    storage behind `Arc`s — with the mutable parts (the delta `Overlay`, the append-only
    dictionary tail, the numeric-cache tail) either cloned (small, O(pending updates)) or
    made copy-on-write.
  - The server then keeps ONE master `Graph`, `update_in_place`s it (µs), and publishes
    `Arc::new(master.snapshot())` per commit. The publish slot stays
    `RwLock<Arc<Graph>>` + single-writer mutex; only the Writer's buffer juggling collapses.

REQUIREMENTS the API must meet:
  1. Snapshots are O(overlay), NEVER O(triples).
  2. Immutable and `Send + Sync`.
  3. Unaffected by later `update_in_place`/`compact` on the master — compaction must not
     invalidate live snapshots (the new base goes into FRESH `Arc`s).

COST / why it is structural (not an additive seam): meeting (1)–(3) means moving
`TripleStore`'s permutation storage and the dictionary's compacted arena behind `Arc`s — a
change to EVERY storage mode, including mmap + compressed. This is why sq-dfs / sq-6h8 /
sq-j39 are all blocked on it.

WINS over the current server double-buffer: removes the ~2x graph residency; removes the
one-time O(graph) rebuild the first update pays to materialise the second buffer (and the
re-pay after a failed update); removes the spare-reclaim wait/rebuild fallback when a
reader holds a snapshot past the query budget.

title: GUI: optional File System Access API path so a re-opened workspace can re-read its original local file (degraded today)
description: Follow-up to sq-atb0 (PR #965). Documented limitation: a local-file import cannot be silently re-read across sessions — the browser keeps no persistent file handle, so on re-open a workspace re-hydrates a LOCAL source from its N-Quads snapshot, not from the original file on disk (URL sources are re-fetchable; local ones are not). The snapshot IS the durable copy and the panel says so plainly, so this is honest, not broken. A future uplift: on a supporting browser, capture a FileSystemFileHandle via the (non-static, permission-gated) File System Access API when a file is picked, persist the handle (IndexedDB), and on re-open re-request permission + re-read the live file so edits to the source on disk flow through. Strictly opt-in + feature-detected (Chromium-only today; Firefox/Safari lack showOpenFilePicker), and never a silent read without a fresh user gesture. In the Tauri desktop app the cleaner path is a native file path + the fs plugin (rides sq-ixc3.6). Low priority — the snapshot cache already makes workspaces durable. [OPUS-4.8]

title: [DEFERRED] Persistent build-time statistics catalog (histograms/cardinality, explicit ANALYZE) wired into goo_pick — #911
description:
DEFERRED per jeswr on issue #911: 'Lets defer this decision until we have more data to base this on.' DO NOT START IMPLEMENTATION. Blocked on canonical measured evidence + on resolving the open design question (see needs_user).

Proposal (SPARQ-agent research, NOT jeswr): a persistent per-predicate statistics catalog (object/subject histograms or quantiles, correlated-predicate join counts), built by an explicit build-time ANALYZE, serialised next to the sparq-core mmap store with a version/fingerprint tag (invalidate on rebuild), and used to seed the planner's goo_pick instead of independence-product marginals. Target surface: sparq-engine planner (goo_pick seed, exec.rs / cs_gate.rs) + sparq-core for mmap serialisation.

CONSTRAINTS (must survive to any future implementer): (1) DEFERRED/benchmark-gated — the verdict is literally 'wait for more data', so this needs canonical numbers showing the catalog beats today's range-probe marginals + the existing opt-in in-RAM characteristic sets on correlated BGPs; the session work-box is NON-CANONICAL and cannot produce the deciding measurements. (2) Opt-in crate/feature — engine stays buildable as pure SPARQL with the catalog absent (mirror existing cs-planner feature). (3) Scope honesty — characteristic sets ALREADY exist but are opt-in, caller-built, in-RAM, thread-local-per-execution (crates/sparq-engine/src/cs.rs); the DELTA is persistence + auto-build + histogram breadth + mmap serialisation, NOT CS itself; v1 = build-time/explicit-ANALYZE, NOT incremental auto-maintenance (the expensive part). (4) Stale catalog degrades estimates only, never correctness (version/fingerprint, invalidate on graph rebuild). (5) Catalog only changes JOIN ORDER; results identical with/without.

Reopen ONLY after jeswr decides the v1-vs-auto-maintenance question AND there is canonical evidence.

title: Agent-effectiveness Phase 1: ast-grep SKILL + outline-reading discipline + the Phase-1 A/B (gated on the baseline)
description:
The highest-ROI low-risk navigation upgrade, adopted ONLY if it passes the shared A/B verdict (research/dogfooding-sparq-knowledge-graph.md §5.6).

1. .claude/skills/ast-grep/SKILL.md + example rules for the 30-crate / ~606-file Rust workspace (find impls of trait X; calls to fn Y with pattern Z). If the ast-grep-mcp server is used it MUST load behind Tool-Search deferral (prefix-tax reject, §1.6).
2. Outline -> skeleton -> selective-read discipline into sparq-rust-feature.md + sparq-researcher.md: files >200 lines, get an outline/signatures first, read only needed sections.
3. A/B ast-grep vs grep on a frozen pattern-heavy task set per the shared §5 protocol; bind the §1.3 first-shot composite as the quality guard; adopt iff the §5.6 verdict returns recommend_adopt.
acceptance_criteria: SKILL.md committed with the install/verify step + the sg-collision guard + full 'ast-grep' invocation in every example; outline discipline added to the two role briefs; A/B run per shared §5 and the verdict object recorded (runtime-only); adopted ONLY on recommend_adopt.
